Natural_Language: Disproportionate employment ratios of laborers, apprentices, or trainees, to journeyman.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_404_1_f_1_v: Particular attention to disproportionate employment ratios.
Validation_Notes: Advisory item ('should'). Compliance focus area. Ratio monitoring between classifications.

Natural_Language: Contractor payroll records in the Government's possession must be carefully protected from any public disclosure which is not required by law, since payroll records may contain information in which the contractor's employees have a privacy interest, as well as information in which the contractor may have a proprietary interest that the Government may be obliged to protect. Questions concerning release of this information may involve the Freedom of Information Act (FOIA).
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_404_1_f_2_a: Payroll records must be protected from public disclosure not required by law; P_22_404_1_f_2_b: Records may contain employee privacy interests; P_22_404_1_f_2_c: Records may contain contractor proprietary interests; P_22_404_1_f_2_d: FOIA may apply to release questions
Validation_Notes: Mandatory protection obligation with declarative context. First atomic is mandatory ('must'). Remaining atomics are informational/declarative providing rationale.

Natural_Language: Apprentice/trainee record review.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_404_1_f_3 = Parent for apprentice/trainee compliance review.
Validation_Notes: Parent aggregating review obligation and corrective action.

Natural_Language: The contracting officer must review the contractor's employment and payment records of apprentices and trainees made available pursuant to the clause at 52.222-8, Payrolls and Basic Records, to ensure that the contractor has complied with the clause at 52.222-9, Apprentices and Trainees.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_404_1_f_3_i_a: CO must review apprentice/trainee employment and payment records per 52.222-8; P_22_404_1_f_3_i_b: Review purpose is to ensure compliance with 52.222-9
Validation_Notes: Mandatory review obligation. Cross-references both 52.222-8 (records source) and 52.222-9 (compliance standard).

Natural_Language: If a contractor has classified employees as apprentices or trainees without complying with the requirements of the clause at 52.222-9, the contracting officer must reject the classification and require the contractor to pay the affected employees at the rates applicable to the classification of the work actually performed.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_404_1_f_3_ii_a: Contractor classified employees as apprentices/trainees without 52.222-9 compliance; P_22_404_1_f_3_ii_b: CO must reject the classification; P_22_404_1_f_3_ii_c: CO must require payment at actual work classification rates
Validation_Notes: Non-compliance triggers two mandatory corrective actions: reject classification AND require proper payment.

Natural_Language: For purposes of the clause at 52.222-6, if the interested parties (i.e. contractor, contracting officer, and employees or their representative) cannot agree on the 'cash equivalent,' the contracting officer must submit the question for final determination to the Department of Labor as prescribed by agency procedures. The information submitted must include a comparison of payments/contributions/costs in the WD with those made or proposed by the contractor, and the comments and recommendations of the contracting officer.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_404_1_g_a: Interested parties cannot agree on cash equivalent under 52.222-6; P_22_404_1_g_b: CO must submit question to DOL per agency procedures; P_22_404_1_g_c: Submission must include comparison of WD payments with contractor's payments/proposals; P_22_404_1_g_d: Submission must include CO comments and recommendations
Validation_Notes: Disagreement on cash equivalent triggers mandatory DOL referral with three content requirements.

Natural_Language: Modifying a contract to exercise an option to extend the term.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_404_1_h = Parent for option extension WD procedures.
Validation_Notes: Parent aggregating six subsections on option extension wage determination procedures.

Natural_Language: Each time the contracting officer exercises an option to extend the term of a contract for construction, or a contract that includes substantial and segregable construction work, the contracting officer must modify the contract to incorporate the most current wage determination.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_404_1_h_1_a: CO exercises option to extend construction contract or contract with substantial/segregable construction; P_22_404_1_h_1_b: CO must modify contract to incorporate most current WD
Validation_Notes: Option exercise triggers mandatory WD incorporation.

Natural_Language: Modified wage determination effective if conditions met.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_404_1_h_2 = Parent for WD effectiveness conditions.
Validation_Notes: Parent with disjunctive structure. Either condition satisfies effectiveness.

Natural_Language: The contracting agency receives a written action from the Department of Labor prior to exercise of the option, or within 45 days after submission of a wage determination request whichever is later.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_404_1_h_2_i_a: Agency receives written DOL action before option exercise; P_22_404_1_h_2_i_b: Agency receives written DOL action within 45 days of WD request; P_22_404_1_h_2_i_c: Whichever is later applies; P_22_404_1_h_2_i_d: Modified WD is effective
Validation_Notes: Disjunctive timing conditions with 'whichever is later' qualifier. Either receipt path triggers effectiveness. The 'later' qualifier means the effective deadline is the more generous of the two.

Natural_Language: The Department of Labor publishes the modification to a general wage determination on the Wage Determinations at SAM.gov before exercise of the option.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_404_1_h_2_ii_a: DOL publishes WD modification on SAM.gov before option exercise; P_22_404_1_h_2_ii_b: Modified WD is effective
Validation_Notes: Publication before option exercise triggers effectiveness.

Natural_Language: If the contracting officer receives an effective modified wage determination either before or after execution of the contract modification to exercise the option, the contracting officer must modify the contract to incorporate the modified wage determination, and any changed wage rates, effective as of the date that the option to extend was effective.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_404_1_h_3_a: CO receives effective modified WD (before or after option execution); P_22_404_1_h_3_b: CO must modify contract to incorporate modified WD; P_22_404_1_h_3_c: Changed wage rates effective as of option effective date
Validation_Notes: Receipt of effective modified WD triggers mandatory incorporation with retroactive effective date. Timing of receipt (before/after execution) does not change obligation.

Natural_Language: The contracting officer must select the most current wage determination(s) from the same schedule(s) as the wage determination(s) incorporated into the contract.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_404_1_h_4_a: CO must select most current WD; P_22_404_1_h_4_b: Selection from same schedule(s) as original contract WD
Validation_Notes: Two conjunctive requirements: currency AND schedule consistency.

Natural_Language: If a contract with an option to extend the term of the contract has indefinite-delivery or indefinite-quantity construction requirements, the contracting officer must incorporate the wage determination incorporated into the contract at the exercise of the option into task orders issued during that option period. The wage determination will be effective for the complete period of performance of those task orders without further revision.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_404_1_h_5_a: IDIQ construction contract with option to extend; P_22_404_1_h_5_b: CO must incorporate option-exercise WD into task orders during option period; P_22_404_1_h_5_c: WD effective for complete TO performance without further revision
Validation_Notes: IDIQ-specific rule. WD at option exercise flows to all task orders in that period and locks for full TO performance. No mid-TO WD updates.

Natural_Language: The contracting officer must include in fixed-price contracts a clause that specifies one of the following methods to provide an allowance for increases or decreases in labor costs from current wage determination at option exercise.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_404_1_h_6 = Parent for fixed-price price adjustment methods.
Validation_Notes: Parent with disjunctive structure. CO must select one of four methods.

Natural_Language: The contracting officer may provide the offerors the opportunity to bid or propose separate prices for each option period. The contracting officer must not further adjust the contract price as a result of the incorporation of a new or revised wage determination at the exercise of each option to extend the term of the contract. Generally, this method is used in construction-only contracts (with options to extend the term) that are not expected to exceed a total of 3 years.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_404_1_h_6_i_a: CO may provide opportunity to bid/propose separate prices per option period; P_22_404_1_h_6_i_b: CO must not further adjust price at option exercise for new WD; P_22_404_1_h_6_i_c: Generally used for construction-only contracts not exceeding 3 years total
Justification_Rules: Tautology (Taut): Rule 18; Negation (Neg): Rule 10; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7
Validation_Notes: 'May' = discretion on offering separate pricing. 'Must not' = prohibition on further adjustment. Advisory guidance on typical use case. Method (i): separate pricing.

Natural_Language: The contracting officer may include in the contract a separately specified pricing method that permits an adjustment to the contract price or contract labor unit price at the exercise of each option to extend the term of the contract. At the time of option exercise, the contracting officer must incorporate a new wage determination into the contract, and must apply the specific pricing method to calculate the contract price adjustment. The contracting officer must not further adjust the contract price as a result of the incorporation of the new or revised wage determination.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_404_1_h_6_ii_a: CO may include separately specified pricing method; P_22_404_1_h_6_ii_b: At option exercise CO must incorporate new WD; P_22_404_1_h_6_ii_c: CO must apply specified pricing method to calculate adjustment; P_22_404_1_h_6_ii_d: CO must not further adjust price beyond method result
Justification_Rules: Tautology (Taut): Rule 18; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Negation (Neg): Rule 10
Validation_Notes: 'May' for method selection, 'must' for incorporation and application, 'must not' for further adjustment. Method (ii): specified pricing formula.

Natural_Language: The contracting officer may provide for a contract price adjustment based solely on a percentage rate determined by the contracting officer using a published economic indicator incorporated into the solicitation and resulting contract. At the exercise of each option, the CO will apply the percentage rate to the portion of contract price designated as labor costs subject to CWRR. The CO must insert 50 percent as the estimated labor portion unless a different percentage is more appropriate. This percentage adjustment must be the only adjustment to cover increases in wages and/or benefits from new or revised WD at option exercise.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_404_1_h_6_iii_a: CO may provide percentage rate adjustment based on published economic indicator; P_22_404_1_h_6_iii_b: At option exercise CO applies percentage to designated labor cost portion; P_22_404_1_h_6_iii_c: Default labor portion is 50 percent unless CO determines different percentage more appropriate before solicitation; P_22_404_1_h_6_iii_d: Percentage adjustment must be only adjustment for wage/benefit changes from new WD
Validation_Notes: 'May' for method selection. 'Will' for application (declarative). 'Must' for 50% default and exclusivity of adjustment. Method (iii): economic indicator percentage.

Natural_Language: The contracting officer may provide a computation method to adjust the contract price to reflect the contractor's actual increase or decrease in wages and fringe benefits (combined) to the extent that the increase is made to comply with, or the decrease is voluntarily made as a result of incorporation of, a new or revised wage determination at the exercise of the option. Generally, this method is appropriate for use only if contract requirements are predominately services subject to the Service Contract Labor Standards statute and the construction requirements are substantial and segregable.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_404_1_h_6_iv_a: CO may provide actual increase/decrease computation method; P_22_404_1_h_6_iv_b: Adjustment reflects contractor's actual wage and fringe benefit changes from new WD at option exercise; P_22_404_1_h_6_iv_c: Generally appropriate only for predominately service contracts with substantial segregable construction
Validation_Notes: 'May' for method selection. Actual-cost basis rather than formula. Advisory guidance on appropriate use cases (predominately services). Method (iv): actual computation.

Natural_Language: Enforcement.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_404_2 = Parent for enforcement requirements.
Validation_Notes: Parent aggregating policy, compliance checking, and investigations.

Natural_Language: Contracting agencies are responsible for ensuring the full and impartial enforcement of labor standards in the administration of construction contracts. Contracting agencies must maintain an effective program that must include the following.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_404_2_a_a: Agencies responsible for full impartial enforcement of labor standards; P_22_404_2_a_b: Agencies must maintain effective enforcement program
Validation_Notes: Parent with embedded mandatory program elements. All four program elements required ('must include').

Natural_Language: Ensuring that contractors and subcontractors are informed, before commencement of work, of their obligations under the labor standards clauses of the contract.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_404_2_a_1: Ensure contractors/subcontractors informed of obligations before work commences.
Validation_Notes: Atomic program element. Pre-work notification obligation.

Natural_Language: Adequate payroll reviews, on-site inspections, and employee interviews to determine compliance by the contractor and subcontractors, and prompt initiation of corrective action when required.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_404_2_a_2_a: Adequate payroll reviews; P_22_404_2_a_2_b: On-site inspections; P_22_404_2_a_2_c: Employee interviews to determine compliance; P_22_404_2_a_2_d: Prompt corrective action when required
Validation_Notes: Four conjunctive program elements for active compliance monitoring and correction.

Natural_Language: Prompt investigation and disposition of complaints.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_404_2_a_3: Prompt investigation and disposition of complaints.
Validation_Notes: Atomic program element. Complaint handling requirement.

Natural_Language: Prompt submission of all reports required by the regulations on labor standards for contracts involving construction in this part.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_404_2_a_4: Prompt submission of all required labor standards reports.
Validation_Notes: Atomic program element. Reporting requirement.

Natural_Language: The contracting officer must make checks and investigations on all contracts covered by this subpart as may be necessary to ensure compliance with the labor standards requirement of the contract.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_404_2_b_a: CO must make checks and investigations on all covered contracts; P_22_404_2_b_b: As necessary to ensure labor standards compliance
Validation_Notes: Parent for compliance checking. Mandatory obligation with necessity qualifier. Covers (b)(1) regular and (b)(2) special checks.

Natural_Language: Regular compliance checks include the following activities.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_404_2_b_1 = Parent for regular compliance check activities.
Validation_Notes: Parent aggregating four regular check activities.

Natural_Language: Employee interviews to determine correctness of classifications, rates of pay, fringe benefits payments, and hours worked. (See Standard Form 1445.)
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_404_2_b_1_i_a: Employee interviews; P_22_404_2_b_1_i_b: Determine correctness of classifications, rates, fringe benefits, hours
Validation_Notes: Interview activity with four compliance verification areas. SF 1445 reference is informational.

Natural_Language: On-site inspections to check type of work performed, number and classification of workers, and fulfillment of posting requirements.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_404_2_b_1_ii_a: On-site inspections; P_22_404_2_b_1_ii_b: Check work type, worker count/classification, posting compliance
Validation_Notes: Inspection activity with three verification areas.

Natural_Language: Payroll reviews to ensure that payrolls of prime contractors and subcontractors have been submitted on time and are complete and in compliance with contract requirements.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_404_2_b_1_iii_a: Payroll reviews; P_22_404_2_b_1_iii_b: Verify timeliness of prime and sub payroll submissions; P_22_404_2_b_1_iii_c: Verify completeness and compliance
Validation_Notes: Payroll review activity with timeliness, completeness, and compliance verification.

Natural_Language: Comparison of the information in this paragraph (b) with available data, including daily inspector's report and daily logs of construction, to ensure consistency.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_404_2_b_1_iv_a: Compare compliance check information with available data; P_22_404_2_b_1_iv_b: Available data includes daily inspector reports and construction logs; P_22_404_2_b_1_iv_c: Purpose is to ensure consistency
Validation_Notes: Cross-validation activity. Data comparison for consistency across sources.

Natural_Language: Situations that may require special compliance checks.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_404_2_b_2 = Parent for special compliance check triggers.
Validation_Notes: Parent with disjunctive structure. Either trigger may require special checks.

Natural_Language: Inconsistencies, errors, or omissions detected during regular compliance checks.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_404_2_b_2_i: Inconsistencies, errors, or omissions from regular checks trigger special checks.
Validation_Notes: Atomic trigger for special compliance check.

Natural_Language: Receipt of a complaint alleging violations. If the complaint is not specific enough, the complainant must be so advised and invited to submit additional information.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_404_2_b_2_ii_a: Complaint alleging violations received; P_22_404_2_b_2_ii_b: Complaint not specific enough; P_22_404_2_b_2_ii_c: Complainant must be advised and invited to submit additional information
Validation_Notes: Complaint receipt is trigger. Conditional: if insufficient specificity, must advise complainant. HIGH-RISK for implication.

Natural_Language: Investigations.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_404_2_c = Parent for investigation requirements.
Validation_Notes: Parent for contracting agency investigation procedures.

Natural_Language: Contracting agencies must conduct an investigation when a compliance check indicates that substantial or willful violations may have occurred or violations have not been corrected.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_404_2_c_1_a: Compliance check indicates substantial/willful violations may have occurred; P_22_404_2_c_1_b: Violations have not been corrected; P_22_404_2_c_1_c: Agency must conduct investigation
Validation_Notes: Disjunctive trigger: substantial/willful violations OR uncorrected violations. Either triggers mandatory investigation. Parent of (c)(1)(i)-(vii).

Natural_Language: Investigation must include the following requirements.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_404_2_c_1_i = Parent for investigation scope requirements.
Validation_Notes: Parent aggregating three mandatory investigation scope elements.

Natural_Language: Include all aspects of the contractor's compliance with contract labor standards requirements.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_404_2_c_1_i_A: Investigation must include all aspects of contractor's labor standards compliance.
Validation_Notes: Atomic. Comprehensive scope requirement.

Natural_Language: Not be limited to specific areas raised in a complaint or uncovered during compliance checks.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_404_2_c_1_i_B: Investigation must not be limited to specific complaint/check areas.
Validation_Notes: Prohibition on narrow scope. Reinforces (A)'s comprehensive requirement.

Natural_Language: Use personnel familiar with labor laws and their application to contracts.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_404_2_c_1_i_C: Investigation must use personnel familiar with labor laws and contract application.
Validation_Notes: Atomic. Personnel qualification requirement.

Natural_Language: Do not disclose contractor employees' oral or written statements taken during an investigation or the employee's identity to anyone other than an authorized Government official without that employee's prior signed consent.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_404_2_c_1_ii_a: Employee statements/identity must not be disclosed; P_22_404_2_c_1_ii_b: Exception: authorized Government official; P_22_404_2_c_1_ii_c: Exception: employee's prior signed consent
Validation_Notes: Prohibition with two exceptions. Default: no disclosure. Exceptions: authorized official OR signed consent.

Natural_Language: Send a written request to the Administrator, Wage and Hour Division, to obtain investigation/enforcement instructions or pertinent DOL files.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_404_2_c_1_iii = Parent for Administrator request options.
Validation_Notes: Parent with disjunctive structure. Two types of requests.

Natural_Language: Investigation and enforcement instructions.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_404_2_c_1_iii_A: Request for investigation and enforcement instructions from Administrator.
Validation_Notes: Atomic. First type of Administrator request.

Natural_Language: Available pertinent Department of Labor files.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_404_2_c_1_iii_B: Request for pertinent DOL files from Administrator.
Validation_Notes: Atomic. Second type of Administrator request.

Natural_Language: Obtain permission from the Department of Labor before disclosing material obtained from Labor Department files, other than computations of back wages and liquidated damages and summaries of back wages due, to anyone other than Government contract administrators.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_404_2_c_1_iv_a: Must obtain DOL permission before disclosing DOL file material; P_22_404_2_c_1_iv_b: Exception: back wage computations and liquidated damages summaries; P_22_404_2_c_1_iv_c: Exception: disclosure to Government contract administrators
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Negation (Neg): Rule 10; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7
Validation_Notes: Permission requirement with two carved-out exceptions. When neither exception applies, DOL permission mandatory. HIGH-RISK for implication with negated antecedent.

Natural_Language: The contracting officer must review the investigation report on receipt and make preliminary findings. The contracting officer normally must not base adverse findings solely on employee statements that the employee does not wish to have disclosed. However, if the investigation establishes a pattern of possible violations that are based on employees' statements that are not authorized for disclosure, the pattern itself may support a finding of noncompliance.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_404_2_c_1_v_a: CO must review investigation report upon receipt; P_22_404_2_c_1_v_b: CO must make preliminary findings; P_22_404_2_c_1_v_c: CO normally must not base adverse findings solely on undisclosable employee statements; P_22_404_2_c_1_v_d: Pattern of violations based on undisclosable statements may support noncompliance finding
Validation_Notes: Three mandatory obligations. Fourth element uses 'may' (pattern-based finding is discretionary). 'Normally must not' introduces qualified prohibition (not absolute). Complex evidentiary standard.

Natural_Language: After completing review, CO must take actions.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_404_2_c_1_vi = Parent for post-review CO actions.
Validation_Notes: Parent aggregating four post-review action requirements.

Natural_Language: Provide the contractor any written preliminary findings and proposed corrective actions, and notice that the contractor has the right to request that the basis for the findings be made available and to submit written rebuttal information.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_404_2_c_1_vi_A_a: Provide written preliminary findings; P_22_404_2_c_1_vi_A_b: Provide proposed corrective actions; P_22_404_2_c_1_vi_A_c: Provide notice of right to request basis for findings; P_22_404_2_c_1_vi_A_d: Provide notice of right to submit written rebuttal
Validation_Notes: Four conjunctive notice requirements. Due process protections for contractor.

Natural_Language: Upon request, provide the contractor with rationale for the findings. However, under no circumstances will the contracting officer permit the contractor to examine the investigation report. Also, the contracting officer must not disclose the identity of any employee who filed a complaint or who was interviewed, without the prior consent of the employee.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_404_2_c_1_vi_B_a: Upon request provide rationale for findings; P_22_404_2_c_1_vi_B_b: Under no circumstances permit contractor to examine investigation report; P_22_404_2_c_1_vi_B_c: Must not disclose employee identity without prior consent
Validation_Notes: Conditional obligation (rationale upon request) plus two absolute prohibitions. 'Under no circumstances' is strongest prohibition language. Employee identity protection reinforces (c)(1)(ii).

Natural_Language: Contractor rebuttal process.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_404_2_c_1_vi_C = Parent for rebuttal procedures.
Validation_Notes: Parent aggregating rebuttal submission and default provisions.

Natural_Language: The contractor may rebut the findings in writing within 60 days after it receives a copy of the preliminary findings. The rebuttal becomes part of the official investigation record. If the contractor submits a rebuttal, evaluate the preliminary findings and notify the contractor of the final findings.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_404_2_c_1_vi_C_1_a: Contractor may rebut in writing within 60 days; P_22_404_2_c_1_vi_C_1_b: Rebuttal becomes part of official record; P_22_404_2_c_1_vi_C_1_c: If rebuttal submitted, CO must evaluate and notify of final findings
Justification_Rules: Tautology (Taut): Rule 18; Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7
Validation_Notes: 'May' = discretionary rebuttal (tautology). If exercised: rebuttal in record AND CO must evaluate and notify. 60-day window.

Natural_Language: If the contracting officer does not receive a timely rebuttal, the contracting officer must consider the preliminary findings final.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_404_2_c_1_vi_C_2_a: No timely rebuttal received; P_22_404_2_c_1_vi_C_2_b: CO must consider preliminary findings final
Validation_Notes: Default rule: no rebuttal = findings finalized. HIGH-RISK for implication.

Natural_Language: If appropriate, request the contractor to make restitution for underpaid wages and assess liquidated damages. If the request includes liquidated damages, the request must state that the contractor has 60 days to request relief from such assessment.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_404_2_c_1_vi_D_a: If appropriate, request restitution for underpaid wages; P_22_404_2_c_1_vi_D_b: If appropriate, assess liquidated damages; P_22_404_2_c_1_vi_D_c: If liquidated damages included, must state contractor has 60 days to request relief
Justification_Rules: Tautology (Taut): Rule 18; Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7
Validation_Notes: 'If appropriate' = discretionary for both restitution and liquidated damages. But if LD assessed, 60-day relief notice is mandatory. Conditional obligation nested in discretionary action.

Natural_Language: After taking actions in (v) and (vi).
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_404_2_c_1_vii = Parent for post-investigation reporting.
Validation_Notes: Parent aggregating CO reporting to agency head and agency head processing.

Natural_Language: The contracting officer must prepare and forward a report of any violations, including findings and supporting evidence, to the agency head. Standard Form 1446, Labor Standards Investigation Summary Sheet, is the first page of the report.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_404_2_c_1_vii_A_a: CO must prepare violation report with findings and evidence; P_22_404_2_c_1_vii_A_b: CO must forward report to agency head; P_22_404_2_c_1_vii_A_c: SF 1446 is first page of report
Validation_Notes: Three conjunctive requirements: prepare, forward, use SF 1446.

Natural_Language: The agency head must process the report.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_404_2_c_1_vii_B = Parent for agency head report processing.
Validation_Notes: Parent for report processing requirements including detailed enforcement report.

Natural_Language: The contracting officer must send a detailed enforcement report to the Administrator, Wage and Hour Division, within 60 days after completion of the investigation, if conditions are met.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_404_2_c_1_vii_B_1 = Parent for enforcement report triggers.
Validation_Notes: Parent with disjunctive structure. Any of three conditions triggers mandatory 60-day enforcement report to Administrator.

Natural_Language: A contractor or subcontractor underpaid by $1,000 or more.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_404_2_c_1_vii_B_1_i_a: Underpayment of $1,000 or more; P_22_404_2_c_1_vii_B_1_i_b: Detailed enforcement report required within 60 days
Validation_Notes: $1,000 threshold triggers mandatory reporting. HIGH-RISK for implication.

Natural_Language: The contracting officer believes that the violations are aggravated or willful (or there is reason to believe that the contractor has disregarded its obligations to employees and subcontractors under the Construction Wage Rate Requirements statute).
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_404_2_c_1_vii_B_1_ii_a: CO believes violations aggravated or willful; P_22_404_2_c_1_vii_B_1_ii_b: Reason to believe contractor disregarded CWRR obligations; P_22_404_2_c_1_vii_B_1_ii_c: Detailed enforcement report required within 60 days
Validation_Notes: Disjunctive belief/reason triggers mandatory reporting. Subjective standard (CO belief or reason to believe).

Natural_Language: The contractor or subcontractor has not made restitution.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_404_2_c_1_vii_B_1_iii_a: Contractor/subcontractor has not made restitution; P_22_404_2_c_1_vii_B_1_iii_b: Detailed enforcement report required within 60 days
Validation_Notes: Failure to make restitution triggers mandatory reporting.

Natural_Language: Future compliance has not been assured.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_406_8_c_1_vii_B_1_iv_a: Future compliance has not been assured
Validation_Notes: Condition (iv) within the list of triggers for forwarding the report. Part of a disjunctive set of conditions under (B)(1). Atomic and self-contained.

Natural_Language: If the Department of Labor expressly requested the investigation and none of the conditions in paragraph (c)(1)(vii)(B)(1) of this subsection exist, submit a summary report to the Administrator, Wage and Hour Division. The report must include the items in (i) through (vi).
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_406_8_c_1_vii_B_2_a: DOL expressly requested the investigation; P_22_406_8_c_1_vii_B_2_b: None of conditions in (c)(1)(vii)(B)(1) exist; P_22_406_8_c_1_vii_B_2_c: Submit summary report to Administrator WHD
Validation_Notes: Conditional: both DOL request AND absence of (B)(1) conditions must hold to trigger report submission. Parent of report content requirements (i)-(vi). HIGH-RISK flagged for implication.

Natural_Language: A summary of any violations.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_406_8_c_1_vii_B_2_i_a: Report includes summary of any violations
Validation_Notes: Mandatory report element when (B)(2) triggered. Atomic requirement.

Natural_Language: The amount of restitution paid.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_406_8_c_1_vii_B_2_ii_a: Report includes amount of restitution paid
Validation_Notes: Mandatory report element. Atomic requirement.

Natural_Language: The number of workers who received restitution.

Natural_Language: Executive Order 11141 nondiscrimination because of age policy (parent).
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_901_1_a: Parent aggregating EO 11141 policy provisions
Validation_Notes: Parent. Three policy provisions from EO 11141.

Natural_Language: Contractors and subcontractors must not, in connection with employment, advancement, or discharge of employees, or the terms, conditions, or privileges of their employment, discriminate against persons because of their age except upon the basis of a bona fide occupational qualification, retirement plan, or statutory requirement.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_901_1_a_a: Contractors/subs discriminate based on age in employment matters; P_22_901_1_a_b: Discrimination based on BFOQ, retirement plan, or statutory requirement
Validation_Notes: Prohibition with exceptions. 'Must not' = prohibition. Three disjunctive exceptions (BFOQ, retirement, statutory). Logic: either no discrimination occurs OR an exception applies.

Natural_Language: Contractors and subcontractors, or persons acting on their behalf, must not specify in solicitations or advertisements for employees to work on Government contracts, a maximum age limit for employment unless the specified maximum age limit is based upon a bona fide occupational qualification, retirement plan, or statutory requirement.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_901_1_b_a: Max age limit specified in solicitations/advertisements; P_22_901_1_b_b: Limit based on BFOQ, retirement plan, or statutory requirement
Validation_Notes: Prohibition with same three exceptions as (a). Applies to solicitations/advertisements. 'Unless' = exception. Logic mirrors (a).

Natural_Language: Agencies will bring this policy to the attention of contractors. The use of contract clauses is not required.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_901_1_c_a: Agencies bring policy to contractors' attention; P_22_901_1_c_b: Contract clauses not required
Validation_Notes: Two atomic statements: notification is declarative ('will'), clause non-requirement is explicit negation. Notable that no clause prescription exists unlike most labor standards.

Natural_Language: Agencies must bring complaints regarding a contractor's compliance with the policy in Executive Order 11141 to that contractor's attention (in writing, if appropriate), stating the policy, indicating that the contractor's compliance has been questioned, and requesting that the contractor take any appropriate steps that may be necessary to comply.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_902_a: Complaint received re contractor compliance with EO 11141; P_22_902_b: Agency brings complaint to contractor's attention; P_22_902_c: Communication states the policy; P_22_902_d: Communication indicates compliance questioned; P_22_902_e: Communication requests appropriate compliance steps
Validation_Notes: Conditional: complaint triggers four-part mandatory response. 'Must' = mandatory. 'In writing, if appropriate' adds discretion on form but not on substance. HIGH-RISK.

Natural_Language: This subpart prescribes policies and procedures implementing the provisions of 41 U.S.C. chapter 67, Service Contract Labor Standards (formerly known as the Service Contract Act of 1965) and related Secretary of Labor regulations and instructions (29 CFR parts 4, 6, 8, and 1925).
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1000_a: Subpart 22.10 implements 41 USC Ch. 67 (SCLS) and related DOL regulations
Validation_Notes: Scope statement. Declarative. Identifies statutory and regulatory authority. External refs to 29 CFR parts 4, 6, 8, 1925. Atomic.

Natural_Language: Definitions for Subpart 22.10 (parent).
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1001_a: Parent aggregating SCLS definitions
Validation_Notes: Parent. Three definitions for subpart.

Natural_Language: Contractor includes a subcontractor at any tier whose subcontract is subject to the provisions of the statute.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1001_def_contractor_a: Contractor defined to include subcontractors at any tier subject to the statute
Validation_Notes: Definitional. Expansive definition including all tiers of subs. Atomic.

Natural_Language: Multiple year contracts means contracts having a term of more than 1 year regardless of fiscal year funding. The term includes multi-year contracts (see 17.102).
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1001_def_multiple_year_a: Multiple year = term more than 1 year regardless of funding; P_22_1001_def_multiple_year_b: Includes multi-year contracts per 17.102
Validation_Notes: Definitional. Conjunctive: base definition AND inclusion of 17.102 multi-year contracts. External dep.

Natural_Language: United States means the 50 States, the District of Columbia, Puerto Rico, the Northern Mariana Islands, American Samoa, Guam, the U.S. Virgin Islands, Johnston Island, Wake Island, and the outer Continental Shelf as defined in the Outer Continental Shelf Lands Act (43 U.S.C. 1331, et seq.), but does not include any other place subject to U.S. jurisdiction or any U.S. base or possession within a foreign country (29 CFR 4.112).
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1001_def_us_a: US includes 50 states, DC, PR, NMI, AS, Guam, USVI, Johnston, Wake, and OCS per 43 USC 1331; P_22_1001_def_us_b: Excludes other places subject to US jurisdiction; P_22_1001_def_us_c: Excludes US bases/possessions in foreign countries
Validation_Notes: Definitional with explicit inclusions and exclusions. Broader than the 22.601-2 geographic scope (which only covers US, PR, USVI). External ref to 29 CFR 4.112 and 43 USC 1331.

Natural_Language: Presolicitation requirements for Service Contract Labor Standards (placeholder - section header only in this segment).
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1002_a: Section 22.1002 continues in subsequent segment
Validation_Notes: Section header only. Content continues in segment 4 of 8. Marked INCOMPLETE pending full text.

Natural_Language: Section 22.1002-1 establishes the applicability of the Service Contract Labor Standards (SCLS) statute, including its scope, statutory exemptions, and Secretarial exemptions.
Validation_Notes: Parent proposition aggregating all applicability provisions. All subsections collectively define SCLS scope.

Natural_Language: [Reserved]
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1002_1_a: Section reserved for future use
Validation_Notes: Reserved section with no operative content. Placeholder only.

Natural_Language: This subpart applies to all Government contracts, the principal purpose of which is to furnish services in the United States through the use of service employees, except as exempted in paragraphs (c) through (g) of this subsection, or any subcontract at any tier thereunder.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1002_1_b_a: Contract's principal purpose is to furnish services in the US through service employees; P_22_1002_1_b_b: Subpart applies to the contract and any subcontract at any tier; P_22_1002_1_b_c: Contract is not exempt under paragraphs (c) through (g)
Validation_Notes: Conditional applicability: principal purpose + non-exempt status triggers SCLS coverage. HIGH-RISK rule 15 used for conditional structure. Exemptions in (c)-(g) function as negating conditions.

Natural_Language: The Service Contract Labor Standards statute does not apply to the contract types listed in paragraphs (c)(1) through (c)(7).
Validation_Notes: Parent for statutory exemptions. Disjunctive: any one exemption is independently sufficient to exclude SCLS applicability.

Natural_Language: Any contract for construction, alteration, or repair of public buildings or public works, including painting and decorating.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1002_1_c_1: Contract is for construction, alteration, or repair of public buildings or public works
Validation_Notes: Statutory exemption. Construction/repair contracts fall under Davis-Bacon, not SCLS. HIGH-RISK rule 15 for implication.

Natural_Language: Any work required to be done in accordance with the provisions of 41 U.S.C. chapter 65.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1002_1_c_2: Work is required under 41 U.S.C. chapter 65 (Walsh-Healey Public Contracts Act)
Validation_Notes: Statutory exemption for Walsh-Healey covered work. Separate labor standards regime applies.

Natural_Language: Any contract for transporting freight or personnel by vessel, aircraft, bus, truck, express, railroad, or oil or gas pipeline where published tariff rates are in effect.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1002_1_c_3_a: Contract is for transporting freight or personnel by specified modes; P_22_1002_1_c_3_b: Published tariff rates are in effect
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Negation (Neg): Rule 10
Validation_Notes: Two conditions must be met: transport contract AND published tariff rates. Both required for exemption.

Natural_Language: Any contract for furnishing services by radio, telephone, or cable companies subject to the Communications Act of 1934.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1002_1_c_4_a: Contract furnishes services by radio, telephone, or cable company; P_22_1002_1_c_4_b: Company is subject to Communications Act of 1934
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Negation (Neg): Rule 10
Validation_Notes: Dual condition: telecom services provider AND subject to Communications Act. Both required.

Natural_Language: Any contract for public utility services.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1002_1_c_5: Contract is for public utility services
Validation_Notes: Straightforward statutory exemption for public utilities.

Natural_Language: Any employment contract providing for direct services to a Federal agency by an individual or individuals.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1002_1_c_6_a: Contract is an employment contract; P_22_1002_1_c_6_b: Contract provides for direct services to a Federal agency by individuals
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Negation (Neg): Rule 10
Validation_Notes: Exempts direct employment relationships, not service contracts through a contractor intermediary.

Natural_Language: Any contract for operating postal contract stations for the U.S. Postal Service.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1002_1_c_7: Contract is for operating postal contract stations for USPS
Validation_Notes: Statutory exemption for USPS postal contract station operations.

Natural_Language: In addition to the statutory exemptions cited in paragraph (c), the Secretary has exempted the following types of contracts from all provisions of the Service Contract Labor Standards statute.
Validation_Notes: Parent for Secretarial administrative exemptions. Disjunctive: any single exemption independently sufficient.

Natural_Language: Contracts entered into by the United States with common carriers for the carriage of mail by rail, air (except air star routes), bus, and ocean vessel, where such carriage is performed on regularly scheduled runs of the trains, airplanes, buses, and vessels over regularly established routes and accounts for an insubstantial portion of the revenue therefrom.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1002_1_d_1_a: Contract is with common carrier for mail carriage by rail, air (except air star routes), bus, or ocean vessel; P_22_1002_1_d_1_b: Carriage is on regularly scheduled runs over regularly established routes; P_22_1002_1_d_1_c: Mail carriage accounts for an insubstantial portion of the carrier's revenue
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Negation (Neg): Rule 10
Validation_Notes: Three conjunctive conditions for mail carrier exemption. 'Insubstantial portion' is subjective and may require DOL guidance. Air star routes explicitly excluded from exemption.

Natural_Language: Any contract entered into by the U.S. Postal Service with an individual owner-operator for mail service if it is not contemplated at the time the contract is made that the owner-operator will hire any service employee to perform the services under the contract except for short periods of vacation time or for unexpected contingencies or emergency situations such as illness, or accident.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1002_1_d_2_a: Contract is between USPS and individual owner-operator for mail service; P_22_1002_1_d_2_b: Not contemplated at contract time that owner-operator will hire service employees; P_22_1002_1_d_2_c: Exception for short vacation periods or unexpected contingencies/emergencies
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Addition (Add): Rule 8; Negation (Neg): Rule 10
Validation_Notes: Owner-operator must be individual. No hiring contemplated at time of contract, with limited exception for temporary coverage. 'Short periods' and 'unexpected contingencies' are qualitative standards.

Natural_Language: Contracts for the carriage of freight or personnel if such carriage is subject to rates covered by section 10721 of the Interstate Commerce Act.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1002_1_d_3_a: Contract is for carriage of freight or personnel; P_22_1002_1_d_3_b: Carriage is subject to rates under section 10721 of the Interstate Commerce Act
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Negation (Neg): Rule 10
Validation_Notes: Dual condition: freight/personnel transport AND ICC rate coverage. Note overlap with statutory exemption at (c)(3) but this adds ICC rate-regulated carriage specifically.

Natural_Language: The Secretary has exempted from the Service Contract Labor Standards statute contracts and subcontracts in which the primary purpose is to furnish maintenance, calibration, or repair of certain types of equipment, subject to conditions at paragraph (e)(2) and procedures at (e)(3) and (e)(4).
Validation_Notes: Parent aggregating equipment maintenance exemption: covered equipment types (e)(1), qualifying conditions (e)(2), source selection procedures (e)(3), and post-award DOL determination procedures (e)(4).

Natural_Language: The Secretary has exempted contracts for maintenance, calibration, or repair of the following types of equipment, if the conditions at paragraph (e)(2) are met.
Validation_Notes: Disjunctive equipment types (any qualifies) conjunctive with mandatory conditions at (e)(2).

Natural_Language: Automated data processing equipment and office information/word processing systems.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1002_1_e_1_i: Contract is for maintenance, calibration, or repair of ADP equipment or office information/word processing systems
Validation_Notes: Equipment type declaration. ADP and word processing systems qualify for exemption consideration.

Natural_Language: Scientific equipment and medical apparatus or equipment if the application of micro-electronic circuitry or other technology of at least similar sophistication is an essential element.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1002_1_e_1_ii_a: Contract is for maintenance/calibration/repair of scientific equipment or medical apparatus; P_22_1002_1_e_1_ii_b: Application of micro-electronic circuitry or similarly sophisticated technology is an essential element
Validation_Notes: Conjunctive: scientific/medical equipment AND sophistication threshold. PSC examples (6515, 6525, 6630, 6655) are illustrative, not exhaustive.

Natural_Language: Office/business machines not otherwise exempt pursuant to paragraph (c)(1)(i) of this subsection, if such services are performed by the manufacturer or supplier of the equipment.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1002_1_e_1_iii_a: Contract is for maintenance/calibration/repair of office/business machines; P_22_1002_1_e_1_iii_b: Equipment is not already exempt under (c)(1)(i); P_22_1002_1_e_1_iii_c: Services performed by manufacturer or supplier
Validation_Notes: Three conjunctive conditions. Manufacturer/supplier performance requirement narrows scope. Cross-reference to (c)(1)(i) avoids double-exemption.

Natural_Language: The exemption at paragraph (e)(1) applies if all the following conditions are met for a contract (or a subcontract).
Validation_Notes: All four conditions mandatory. Conjunctive parent. Failure of any one invalidates the exemption.

Natural_Language: The items of equipment to be serviced under the contract are used regularly for other than Government purposes and are sold or traded by the contractor in substantial quantities to the general public in the course of normal business operations.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1002_1_e_2_i_a: Equipment is used regularly for non-Government purposes; P_22_1002_1_e_2_i_b: Equipment is sold or traded by contractor in substantial quantities to the general public in normal business operations
Validation_Notes: Commercial item character test. Both regular non-government use AND substantial public sales required.

Natural_Language: The services will be furnished at prices which are, or are based on, established catalog or market prices for the maintenance, calibration, or repair of such equipment.
Validation_Notes: Disjunctive: either catalog price OR market price satisfies this condition. Definitions follow in (A) and (B).

Natural_Language: An established catalog price is a price included in a catalog price list, schedule, or other form that is regularly maintained by the manufacturer or the contractor, is either published or otherwise available for inspection by customers, and states prices at which sales currently, or were last, made to a significant number of buyers constituting the general public.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1002_1_e_2_ii_A_a: Price is in a catalog/price list/schedule regularly maintained by manufacturer or contractor; P_22_1002_1_e_2_ii_A_b: Price list is published or available for customer inspection; P_22_1002_1_e_2_ii_A_c: Prices reflect current or most recent sales to a significant number of general public buyers
Validation_Notes: Definitional. Three conjunctive elements define 'established catalog price' per 29 CFR 4.123(e)(1)(ii)(B).

Natural_Language: An established market price is a current price, established in the usual course of trade between buyers and sellers free to bargain, which can be substantiated from sources independent of the manufacturer or contractor.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1002_1_e_2_ii_B_a: Price is current and established in usual course of trade; P_22_1002_1_e_2_ii_B_b: Buyers and sellers are free to bargain; P_22_1002_1_e_2_ii_B_c: Price can be substantiated from independent sources
Validation_Notes: Definitional. Three conjunctive elements define 'established market price' per 29 CFR 4.123(e)(1)(ii)(B).

Natural_Language: The contractor will use the same compensation (wage and fringe benefits) plan for all service employees performing work under the contract as the contractor uses for these employees and equivalent employees servicing the same equipment of commercial customers.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1002_1_e_2_iii: Contractor uses same compensation plan for service employees on government contract as for equivalent employees servicing commercial customers
Validation_Notes: Compensation parity requirement. Prevents wage discrimination between government and commercial service employees.

Natural_Language: The apparent successful offeror certifies to the conditions in paragraph (c)(2)(i) through (iii) of the provision at 52.222-48, Exemption from Application of the Service Contract Labor Standards to Contracts for Maintenance, Calibration, or Repair of Certain Equipment--Certification.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1002_1_e_2_iv: Apparent successful offeror certifies to conditions (c)(2)(i)-(iii) of provision 52.222-48
Validation_Notes: Certification requirement. Cross-references FAR clause 52.222-48. External dependency on Part 52.

Natural_Language: Procedures for contracting officer determination of exemption applicability during source selection and before contract award.
Validation_Notes: Parent for three procedural requirements governing source selection and award determination.

Natural_Language: For source selections where the contracting officer has established a competitive range, if the contracting officer determines that one or more of the conditions in paragraphs (e)(2)(i) through (iii) of an offeror's certification will not be met, the contracting officer must identify the deficiency to the offeror before receipt of the final proposal revisions. Unless the offeror provides a revised offer acknowledging applicability of the Service Contract Labor Standards statute or demonstrating to the satisfaction of the contracting officer an ability to meet all required conditions for exemption, the offer will not be further considered for award.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1002_1_e_3_i_a: CO has established competitive range; P_22_1002_1_e_3_i_b: CO determines conditions (e)(2)(i)-(iii) will not be met; P_22_1002_1_e_3_i_c: CO identifies deficiency to offeror before final proposal revisions; P_22_1002_1_e_3_i_d: Offeror provides revised offer acknowledging SCLS applicability or demonstrating ability to meet exemption conditions; P_22_1002_1_e_3_i_e: Offer will not be considered for award
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Negation (Neg): Rule 10
Validation_Notes: Two-stage conditional: (1) competitive range + deficiency finding triggers notification duty, (2) failure to cure triggers exclusion. Complex multi-implication structure.

Natural_Language: The contracting officer must determine in writing the applicability of this exemption to the contract before contract award. If the apparent successful offeror will meet all conditions in paragraph (e)(2) of this subsection, the contracting officer must make an affirmative determination and award the contract without the otherwise applicable Service Contract Labor Standards clause(s).
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1002_1_e_3_ii_a: CO determines in writing exemption applicability before award; P_22_1002_1_e_3_ii_b: Apparent successful offeror meets all (e)(2) conditions; P_22_1002_1_e_3_ii_c: CO makes affirmative determination; P_22_1002_1_e_3_ii_d: Contract awarded without SCLS clauses
Validation_Notes: Mandatory written determination before award. Conditions met triggers affirmative determination AND SCLS clause exclusion.

Natural_Language: If the apparent successful offeror does not certify to the conditions in paragraph (e)(2)(i) through (iii) of this subsection, the contracting officer must incorporate in the contract the Service Contract Labor Standards clause (see 22.1002-2(b)) and, if the contract will exceed $2,500, the appropriate Department of Labor wage determination (see 22.1002-3).
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1002_1_e_3_iii_a: Apparent successful offeror does not certify to (e)(2)(i)-(iii) conditions; P_22_1002_1_e_3_iii_b: CO incorporates SCLS clause in contract; P_22_1002_1_e_3_iii_c: Contract exceeds $2,500; P_22_1002_1_e_3_iii_d: CO incorporates DOL wage determination
Validation_Notes: Failure to certify triggers SCLS clause inclusion. Nested conditional for wage determination threshold at $2,500.

Natural_Language: Procedures when the Department of Labor determines after award that exemption conditions have not been met.
Validation_Notes: Parent for post-award DOL enforcement provisions covering both prime contracts and subcontracts.

Natural_Language: If the Department of Labor determines after award of the contract that any condition for exemption in paragraph (e)(2) of this subsection has not been met, the exemption shall be deemed inapplicable, and the contract must become subject to the Service Contract Labor Standards statute, effective as of the date of the Department of Labor determination. In such case, the procedures at 29 CFR 4.123(e)(1)(iv) and 29 CFR 4.5(c) must be followed.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1002_1_e_4_i_a: DOL determines after award that (e)(2) condition not met; P_22_1002_1_e_4_i_b: Exemption deemed inapplicable; P_22_1002_1_e_4_i_c: Contract becomes subject to SCLS effective date of DOL determination; P_22_1002_1_e_4_i_d: Procedures at 29 CFR 4.123(e)(1)(iv) and 29 CFR 4.5(c) followed
Validation_Notes: DOL post-award finding triggers three mandatory consequences. Effective date is DOL determination date, not contract award date. External regulatory cross-references to 29 CFR.

Natural_Language: If the Department of Labor determines that any conditions in paragraph (e)(2) of this subsection have not been met with respect to a subcontract, the exemption must be deemed inapplicable. The contractor may be responsible for ensuring that the subcontractor complies with the Service Contract Labor Standards statute, effective as of the date of the subcontract award.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1002_1_e_4_ii_a: DOL determines (e)(2) conditions not met for subcontract; P_22_1002_1_e_4_ii_b: Exemption deemed inapplicable for subcontract; P_22_1002_1_e_4_ii_c: Contractor may be responsible for subcontractor SCLS compliance; P_22_1002_1_e_4_ii_d: Effective date is subcontract award date
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Tautology (Taut): Rule 18
Validation_Notes: 'May be responsible' is permissive/discretionary regarding contractor flow-down liability. Modeled as tautology. Note different effective date (subcontract award) vs prime contract (DOL determination).

Natural_Language: The Secretary has exempted contracts and subcontracts in which the primary purpose is to provide certain enumerated services, subject to conditions, except as provided in paragraph (f)(5).
Validation_Notes: Parent aggregating certain services exemption framework: service types (f)(1), conditions (f)(2), award procedures (f)(3), post-award DOL (f)(4), and exclusions (f)(5).

Natural_Language: Except as provided in paragraph (f)(5), the Secretary has exempted contracts and subcontracts in which the primary purpose is to provide the following services, if the conditions in paragraph (f)(2) are met.
Justification_Rules: Addition (Add): Rule 8; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Negation (Neg): Rule 10
Validation_Notes: Disjunctive service types, conjunctive with conditions and non-exclusion. Any one service type qualifies, all conditions must be met, and (f)(5) exclusions must not apply.

Natural_Language: Automobile or other vehicle (e.g., aircraft) maintenance services (other than contracts or subcontracts to operate a Government motor pool or similar facility).
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1002_1_f_1_i_a: Contract is for vehicle maintenance services; P_22_1002_1_f_1_i_b: Contract is not for operating a Government motor pool or similar facility
Validation_Notes: Vehicle maintenance qualifies but motor pool operation contracts are excluded from exemption.

Natural_Language: Financial services involving the issuance and servicing of cards (including credit cards, debit cards, purchase cards, smart cards, and similar card services).
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1002_1_f_1_ii: Contract is for financial services involving issuance and servicing of cards
Validation_Notes: Card services enumeration is illustrative ('including'). Covers credit, debit, purchase, smart, and similar.

Natural_Language: Hotel/motel services for conferences, including lodging and/or meals, that are part of the contract or subcontract for the conference (which must not include ongoing contracts for lodging on an as needed or continuing basis).
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1002_1_f_1_iii_a: Contract is for hotel/motel conference services including lodging and/or meals; P_22_1002_1_f_1_iii_b: Services are part of a conference contract; P_22_1002_1_f_1_iii_c: Contract is not for ongoing lodging on as-needed or continuing basis
Validation_Notes: Conference-tied lodging only. Ongoing/continuing lodging contracts explicitly excluded from this exemption.

Natural_Language: Maintenance, calibration, repair, and/or installation (where the installation is not subject to the Construction Wage Rate Requirements statute, as provided in 29 CFR 4.116(c)(2)) services for all types of equipment where the services are obtained from the manufacturer or supplier of the equipment under a contract awarded on a sole source basis.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1002_1_f_1_iv_a: Contract is for maintenance/calibration/repair/installation of equipment; P_22_1002_1_f_1_iv_b: Installation is not subject to Construction Wage Rate Requirements statute; P_22_1002_1_f_1_iv_c: Services obtained from manufacturer or supplier; P_22_1002_1_f_1_iv_d: Contract awarded on sole source basis
Validation_Notes: Four conjunctive conditions. Sole source + manufacturer/supplier performance required. Davis-Bacon installation excluded.

Natural_Language: Transportation by common carrier of persons by air, motor vehicle, rail, or marine vessel on regularly scheduled routes or via standard commercial services (not including charter services).
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1002_1_f_1_v_a: Contract is for common carrier transportation of persons by air, motor vehicle, rail, or marine vessel; P_22_1002_1_f_1_v_b: Transportation is on regularly scheduled routes or via standard commercial services; P_22_1002_1_f_1_v_c: Contract does not include charter services
Validation_Notes: Regularly scheduled/standard commercial transport only. Charter services explicitly excluded.

Natural_Language: Real estate services, including real property appraisal services, related to housing Federal agencies or disposing of real property owned by the Government.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1002_1_f_1_vi_a: Contract is for real estate services; P_22_1002_1_f_1_vi_b: Services relate to housing Federal agencies or disposing of Government real property
Validation_Notes: Scope limited to Federal housing and Government property disposal. Appraisal services illustrative.

Natural_Language: Relocation services, including services of real estate brokers and appraisers to assist Federal employees or military personnel in buying and selling homes (which must not include actual moving or storage of household goods and related services).
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1002_1_f_1_vii_a: Contract is for relocation services assisting Federal employees or military in buying/selling homes; P_22_1002_1_f_1_vii_b: Contract does not include actual moving or storage of household goods
Validation_Notes: Relocation assistance only. Physical moving/storage services explicitly excluded from exemption.

Natural_Language: The exemption for the services in paragraph (f)(1) applies if all the following conditions are met for a contract (or for a subcontract).
Validation_Notes: All seven conditions mandatory. Conjunctive parent. Failure of any one invalidates the exemption.

Natural_Language: Either: (A) Except for services identified in paragraph (f)(1)(iv), the contractor will be selected for award based on other factors in addition to price or cost, with the combination of other factors at least as important as price or cost; or (B) The contract will be awarded on a sole source basis.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1002_1_f_2_i_A: Selection based on other factors at least as important as price/cost (except (f)(1)(iv) services); P_22_1002_1_f_2_i_B: Contract awarded sole source
Validation_Notes: Disjunctive: best value OR sole source. (f)(1)(iv) services already require sole source, so (A) exception for them is logical.

Natural_Language: The services under the contract are offered and sold regularly to non-Governmental customers, and are provided by the contractor (or subcontractor in the case of an exempt subcontract) to the general public in substantial quantities in the course of normal business operations.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1002_1_f_2_ii_a: Services offered and sold regularly to non-Government customers; P_22_1002_1_f_2_ii_b: Services provided to general public in substantial quantities in normal business operations
Validation_Notes: Commercial services character test. Both regular non-government sales AND substantial public volume required.

Natural_Language: The contract services are furnished at prices that are, or are based on, established catalog or market prices, as defined at 29 CFR 4.123(e)(2)(ii)(C).
Validation_Notes: Disjunctive: catalog price OR market price. Same definitional structure as (e)(2)(ii).

Natural_Language: An established catalog price is a price included in a catalog, price list, schedule, or other form that is regularly maintained by the contractor, is either published or otherwise available for inspection by customers, and states prices at which sales are currently, or were last, made to a significant number of buyers constituting the general public.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1002_1_f_2_iii_A_a: Price in regularly maintained catalog/price list/schedule; P_22_1002_1_f_2_iii_A_b: Published or available for customer inspection; P_22_1002_1_f_2_iii_A_c: Reflects current or most recent sales to significant number of general public buyers
Validation_Notes: Definitional. Mirrors (e)(2)(ii)(A) catalog price definition for services context.

Natural_Language: An established market price is a current price, established in the usual course of trade between buyers and sellers free to bargain, which can be substantiated from sources independent of the manufacturer or contractor.

Natural_Language: If the incumbent contractor enters into a new or revised collective bargaining agreement during the period of the incumbent's performance on the current contract, the terms of the new or revised agreement must not be effective for the purposes of 41 U.S.C. 6707(c) under the following conditions: (A) In sealed bidding, contracting agency receives notice less than 10 days before bid opening and finds insufficient time to notify bidders, or for other contractual actions, agency receives notice after award with start of performance within 30 days; and (B) the CO has given both the incumbent contractor and its employees' CBA agent timely written notification of the applicable acquisition dates.

Validation_Notes: Complex timing limitation. Disjunctive timing triggers (sealed bid vs. other) AND conjunctive CO notification requirement. Cross-refs 22.1003(b) and 22.1004-6.

Natural_Language: If 41 U.S.C. 6707(c) applies, the contracting officer must obtain a copy of any collective bargaining agreement between an incumbent contractor or subcontractor and its employees. Obtaining a copy may involve coordination with the administrative contracting officer responsible for administering the predecessor contract. Paragraph (m) of 52.222-41 requires the incumbent prime to furnish the CO a copy of each CBA.

Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Tautology (Taut): Rule 18
Validation_Notes: 6707(c) applicability triggers CBA procurement duty. ACO coordination is discretionary ('may'). Incumbent's clause obligation provides enforcement mechanism.

Natural_Language: 41 U.S.C. 6707(c) will not apply if the Secretary of Labor determines: (i) after a hearing, that CBA wages/fringe benefits are substantially at variance with those prevailing for similar services in the locality; or (ii) that CBA wages/fringe benefits are not the result of arm's length negotiations.

Validation_Notes: Two independent Secretary-level exceptions. Substantial variance requires hearing; arm's length failure does not explicitly require one. DOL has noted contingent CBA provisions as evidence of non-arm's-length bargaining.

Natural_Language: If the contracting officer's review of the incumbent's collective bargaining agreement indicates that its monetary provisions may be substantially at variance or may not have been reached as a result of arm's length bargaining, the contracting officer must immediately contact the agency labor advisor to consider if further action is warranted.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1002_3_b_6_a: CO review indicates CBA provisions may be at variance or not arm's length; P_22_1002_3_b_6_b: CO immediately contacts agency labor advisor
Validation_Notes: Mandatory escalation upon suspicion. 'Immediately' indicates urgency. 'May be' is a low threshold for triggering the duty to contact the labor advisor.

Natural_Language: If the services are being furnished at more than one location and the collectively bargained wage rates and fringe benefits are different at different locations or do not apply to one or more locations, the contracting officer must identify the locations to which the agreements apply.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1002_3_b_7_a: Services at multiple locations; P_22_1002_3_b_7_b: CBA rates differ by location or do not apply to some locations; P_22_1002_3_b_7_c: CO identifies which locations CBAs apply to
Validation_Notes: Multi-location CBA mapping duty. Both conditions (multi-location AND rate variance) must exist to trigger identification requirement.

Natural_Language: Executive Order 13658 established minimum wages for certain workers at $10.10 per hour. The E.O. 13658 rate has increased each year since 2015, rising to $11.25 on January 1, 2022. As of January 30, 2022, E.O. 13658 is superseded by E.O. 14026 to the extent that it is inconsistent with E.O. 14026; the minimum wage rate for certain workers is increased to $15.00 per hour. The wage rate is subject to annual increases by an amount determined by the Secretary of Labor. The clause at 52.222-55 requires the E.O. 14026 minimum wage rate to be paid if it is higher than other minimum wage rates, such as the subpart 22.10 statutory wage determination amount.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1002_4_a: E.O. 13658 established minimum wage at $10.10/hr for certain workers; P_22_1002_4_b: As of Jan 30 2022 E.O. 14026 supersedes E.O. 13658 where inconsistent; P_22_1002_4_c: E.O. 14026 minimum wage is $15.00/hr; P_22_1002_4_d: Wage rate subject to annual increases determined by Secretary of Labor; P_22_1002_4_e: Clause 52.222-55 requires E.O. 14026 rate to be paid if higher than other minimum wage rates
Validation_Notes: Declarative section establishing EO minimum wage framework. Material implication used for the 52.222-55 clause requirement (higher-rate-applies rule). E.O. supersession is temporal conditional. HIGH-RISK flag for implication on rate comparison logic.

Validation_Notes: First atomic is permissive (may issue). Second is declarative establishing receipt-date rule. Both validated as straightforward regulatory statements.

Natural_Language: For purposes of using Wage Determinations at SAM.gov, the time of receipt by the contracting agency must be the first day of publication of the revised prevailing wage determination on the website.

Validation_Notes: Conditional: using SAM.gov triggers specific receipt date definition. HIGH-RISK for implication but directional logic is clear and unambiguous.

Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1003_a_1_ii: Using e98 process implies receipt date equals date of actual notice from DOL as e98 response
Validation_Notes: Parallel conditional to (a)(1)(i) for e98 process. Receipt date defined differently per process used. HIGH-RISK flag for implication.

Natural_Language: In selecting a prevailing wage determination from SAM.gov for use in a solicitation or other contract action, the contracting officer must monitor SAM.gov to determine whether the applicable wage determination has been revised. Revisions published on SAM.gov or otherwise communicated to the CO within prescribed timeframes are effective and must be included in the resulting contract. Monitoring can be accomplished by use of the Alert Service.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1003_a_2_a: CO must monitor SAM.gov for wage determination revisions when selecting for solicitation/contract action; P_22_1003_a_2_b: Revisions published/communicated within prescribed timeframes are effective and must be included; P_22_1003_a_2_c: Monitoring can be accomplished via Alert Service
Validation_Notes: Mandatory monitoring obligation with permissive method suggestion (Alert Service). Timeframes referenced in (a)(3) and (a)(4) create dependencies.

Natural_Language: The following must apply when contracting by sealed bidding: a revised prevailing wage determination shall not be effective if it is received by the contracting agency less than 10 days before the opening of bids, and the contracting officer finds that there is not reasonable time to incorporate the revision in the solicitation.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1003_a_3_a: Contract is by sealed bidding; P_22_1003_a_3_b: Revised WD received less than 10 days before bid opening; P_22_1003_a_3_c: CO finds no reasonable time to incorporate; P_22_1003_a_3_d: Revised WD is not effective
Validation_Notes: Three conjunctive conditions in antecedent trigger non-effectiveness of revised WD. All three must be true. HIGH-RISK for implication but logic tracks regulatory text directly.

Natural_Language: For contractual actions other than sealed bidding, a revised prevailing wage determination received by the contracting agency after award of a new contract or a modification as specified in 22.1004-1(c) shall not be effective provided that the start of performance is within 30 days of the award or the specified modification. If the contract does not specify a start of performance date within 30 days of award/modification, and if contract performance does not commence within 30 days, any revision received not less than 10 days before commencement of work shall be effective.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1003_a_4_a: Action is other than sealed bidding; P_22_1003_a_4_b: Revised WD received after award/modification; P_22_1003_a_4_c: Start of performance within 30 days of award/modification; P_22_1003_a_4_d: Revised WD not effective; P_22_1003_a_4_e: No specified start date within 30 days AND performance does not commence within 30 days; P_22_1003_a_4_f: Revision received not less than 10 days before commencement; P_22_1003_a_4_g: Revised WD is effective
Validation_Notes: Two conditional pathways: (1) revised WD ineffective if performance starts within 30 days, (2) revised WD effective if delayed start and 10-day notice met. Complex dual-path logic. Cross-reference to 22.1004-1(c).

Natural_Language: If the contracting officer has submitted an e98 to the Department of Labor requesting a prevailing wage determination and has not received a response within 10 days, the contracting officer must contact the Wage and Hour Division by telephone to determine when the wage determination can be expected.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1003_a_5_a: CO submitted e98 to DOL requesting prevailing WD; P_22_1003_a_5_b: No response received within 10 days; P_22_1003_a_5_c: CO must contact WHD by telephone
Validation_Notes: Conditional: e98 submitted AND no response within 10 days triggers mandatory telephone contact. Straightforward procedural requirement.

Natural_Language: Wage determinations based on collective bargaining agreements, covering sealed bidding and other contractual actions timing rules.

Validation_Notes: Parent for CBA-based wage determination subsections.

Natural_Language: In sealed bidding, a new or changed collective bargaining agreement shall not be effective under 41 U.S.C. 6707(c) if the contracting agency has received notice of the terms of the new or changed CBA less than 10 days before bid opening and the contracting officer determines that there is not reasonable time to incorporate the new or changed terms in the solicitation.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1003_b_1_a: Sealed bidding procurement; P_22_1003_b_1_b: Notice of new/changed CBA received less than 10 days before bid opening; P_22_1003_b_1_c: CO determines no reasonable time to incorporate; P_22_1003_b_1_d: New/changed CBA not effective under 41 USC 6707(c)
Validation_Notes: Parallel structure to 22.1003(a)(3) but for CBA-based determinations. Three conjunctive conditions trigger non-effectiveness.

Natural_Language: For contractual actions other than sealed bidding, a new or changed CBA shall not be effective under 41 U.S.C. 6707(c) if notice of terms is received by the contracting agency after award of a successor contract or modification as specified in 22.1004-1(c), provided that the contract start of performance is within 30 days. If no start date within 30 days or performance does not commence within 30 days, any notice received not less than 10 days before commencement must be effective.
