Validation_Notes: Parallel structure to 22.1003(a)(4) for CBA context. Dual conditional pathways. Cross-ref to 22.1004-1(c).

Natural_Language: The limitations in paragraphs (b)(1) and (2) of this section must apply only if timely notification required in 22.1004-6 has been given.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1003_b_3_a: Timely notification per 22.1004-6 has been given; P_22_1003_b_3_b: Limitations in (b)(1) and (b)(2) apply
Validation_Notes: Gating condition: the timing limitations in (b)(1)/(b)(2) only activate if 22.1004-6 notification was given. Without notification, limitations do not apply. Critical dependency.

Natural_Language: If the contracting officer has submitted an e98 to DOL requesting a wage determination based on a CBA and has not received a response within 10 days, the CO must contact WHD by telephone. If DOL is unable to provide the WD by the latest date needed to maintain the acquisition schedule, the CO must incorporate the CBA itself in a solicitation or other contract action and include a wage determination referencing that CBA created by use of SAM.gov.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1003_b_4_a: CO submitted e98 for CBA-based WD; P_22_1003_b_4_b: No response within 10 days; P_22_1003_b_4_c: CO must contact WHD by telephone; P_22_1003_b_4_d: DOL unable to provide WD by latest needed date; P_22_1003_b_4_e: CO must incorporate CBA itself and include SAM.gov-created WD referencing CBA
Validation_Notes: Two sequential conditionals: first triggers telephone contact, second triggers CBA incorporation as fallback. Both are mandatory actions when conditions met.

Natural_Language: If a wage determination was obtained through the e98 process, and bid opening has been delayed more than 60 days from the date indicated on the previously submitted e98, the contracting officer must submit a new e98. Any revision of a wage determination received as a result must supersede the earlier response as the applicable WD subject to the time frames in 22.1003(a)(3) and (4).
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1003_c_a: WD obtained through e98; P_22_1003_c_b: Bid opening delayed more than 60 days from e98 date; P_22_1003_c_c: CO must submit new e98; P_22_1003_c_d: Resulting revision supersedes earlier response
Validation_Notes: Conditional: e98 WD + 60-day delay triggers mandatory new e98 submission and supersession. Dependencies on timing rules in (a)(3)/(a)(4).

Natural_Language: The contracting officer must take steps to ensure that service employees are notified of minimum wages and fringe benefits.
Atomic_Propositions: Parent proposition aggregating 22.1003(d)(1) and 22.1003(d)(2)
Validation_Notes: Parent for notification subsections.

Natural_Language: At the time of award, furnish the contractor DOL Publication WH-1313, Notice to Employees Working on Government Contracts, for posting at a prominent and accessible place at the worksite before contract performance begins. The publication advises employees of compensation required under SCLS and satisfies the notice requirements in paragraph (g) of the clause at 52.222-41.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1003_d_1_a: At award, CO must furnish WH-1313 to contractor; P_22_1003_d_1_b: Must be posted at prominent and accessible place before performance begins; P_22_1003_d_1_c: Publication satisfies notice requirements in 52.222-41(g)
Validation_Notes: Mandatory posting requirement. Three conjunctive obligations. External dependency on clause 52.222-41(g).

Natural_Language: Attach any applicable wage determination to Publication WH-1313.

Validation_Notes: Atomic mandatory requirement. Depends on WH-1313 being furnished per (d)(1).

Natural_Language: Postaward requirements for Service Contract Labor Standards, covering revisions to wage determinations, additional classes of service employees, withholding of contract payments, termination for default, enforcement, notification to interested parties, and seniority lists.
Atomic_Propositions: Parent proposition aggregating 22.1004-1 through 22.1004-7
Validation_Notes: Parent for all postaward subsections.

Natural_Language: Postaward revisions to wage determinations, covering periodic revisions, e98 delays, modifications bringing contracts above $2,500, multi-year contracts, DOL inability to provide WDs, and erroneous determinations.

Validation_Notes: Parent for wage determination revision subsections.

Natural_Language: The Wage and Hour Administrator may issue revisions to prevailing wage determinations periodically. The need for inclusion of a revised prevailing wage determination in a contract is determined by the date of receipt of the revised prevailing wage determination by the contracting agency.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1004_1_a_a: WHD Administrator may issue periodic revisions; P_22_1004_1_a_b: Need for inclusion determined by receipt date at contracting agency
Validation_Notes: Permissive authority (may) for administrator plus declarative receipt-date rule. Parallel to pre-award 22.1003(a)(1).

Natural_Language: If a wage determination was obtained through the e98 process, and commencement of work under a negotiated contract has been delayed more than 60 days from the date indicated on the previously submitted e98, the contracting officer must submit a new e98. Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1004_1_b_a: WD obtained through e98; P_22_1004_1_b_b: Commencement delayed more than 60 days from e98 date; P_22_1004_1_b_c: CO must submit new e98; P_22_1004_1_b_d: Resulting revision supersedes earlier response

Validation_Notes: Parent: CO must obtain WDs when modifications bring contract above $2,500 under two conditions.

Natural_Language: The contracting officer must obtain wage determinations for each contract modification which brings the contract above $2,500 and extends the existing contract pursuant to an option clause or otherwise.

Validation_Notes: Conditional: two conditions (above $2,500 AND extension) trigger WD obligation.

Validation_Notes: Parent for multi-year contract WD timing.

Validation_Notes: Conditional: multi-year + annual appropriations = annual WD refresh requirement.

Natural_Language: If the contracting officer has submitted an e98 to DOL requesting a wage determination based on a CBA and the DOL is unable to provide the WD by the latest date needed to maintain the acquisition schedule, the CO must incorporate the CBA itself in a contract action and include a wage determination referencing that CBA created by use of SAM.gov.

Natural_Language: If the DOL discovers and determines, whether before or after a contract award, that a CO made an erroneous determination that SCLS did not apply or failed to include an appropriate wage determination, the CO within 30 days of notification must include clause 52.222-41 and any applicable wage determination. Validation_Notes: DOL error discovery triggers mandatory correction within 30 days plus equitable adjustment. Retroactive application is permissive (may) modeled as tautology. Complex multi-obligation consequent.

Natural_Language: Requirements for classifying service employees not included in wage determinations, including conforming procedures, restrictions on trainee and helper classifications, and subminimum rate provisions.
Atomic_Propositions: Parent proposition aggregating 22.1004-2(a) through 22.1004-2(c)
Validation_Notes: Parent for additional classes subsections.

Natural_Language: If the CO is aware that contract performance involves classes of service employees not included in the wage determination, the CO must require the contractor to classify the unlisted classes to provide a reasonable relationship between unlisted and listed classifications. The contractor must initiate the conforming procedure before unlisted classes perform contract work. The contractor must submit SF 1444. The CO must review and promptly submit the completed SF 1444 with all pertinent information to the WHD. Within 30 days the WHD will approve, modify, or disapprove when parties agree, or render final determination in disagreement.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1004_2_a_a: CO aware of unlisted service employee classes; P_22_1004_2_a_b: CO must require contractor to classify unlisted classes with reasonable relationship to listed; P_22_1004_2_a_c: Contractor must initiate conforming before unlisted classes perform; P_22_1004_2_a_d: Contractor must submit SF 1444; P_22_1004_2_a_e: CO must review and submit SF 1444 to WHD; P_22_1004_2_a_f: WHD acts within 30 days
Validation_Notes: Conditional: CO awareness triggers multi-step conforming procedure. Five mandatory sequential obligations. Cross-ref to 52.222-41(c).

Natural_Language: Some wage determinations list classes within a job classification family at multiple levels. Level I is entry level and establishment of a lower level through conformance is not permissible. Trainee classifications may not be conformed. Helpers in skilled maintenance trades may be used if listed but may not be conformed. Conformance may not be used to artificially split or subdivide listed classifications. Conforming procedures may be used if work performed is not within scope of any listed classification regardless of job title.

Validation_Notes: Parent aggregating OFCCP Director waiver, agency head waiver, submission procedures, and withdrawal provisions.

Natural_Language: The Director of OFCCP may waive the application of any or all of the terms of the clause at 52.222-36 for any contract if deemed in the national interest, or for groups or categories of contracts if in the national interest and it is impracticable to act individually and the waiver will substantially contribute to convenience in administering the Act.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1401_3_a: Parent for OFCCP Director waiver authority
Validation_Notes: Disjunctive: either individual contract waiver or group/category waiver pathway. Both require national interest.

Natural_Language: The Director of OFCCP may waive for any contract if a waiver is deemed to be in the national interest.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1401_3_a_1_a: Waiver deemed in national interest; P_22_1401_3_a_1_b: Director may waive for individual contract
Validation_Notes: National interest is necessary condition; waiver itself discretionary ("may"). Tautology for discretion.

Natural_Language: The Director of OFCCP may waive for groups or categories of contracts if a waiver is in the national interest and it is impracticable to act on each request individually and the waiver will substantially contribute to convenience in administering the Act.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1401_3_a_2_a: Waiver in national interest; P_22_1401_3_a_2_b: Impracticable to act individually; P_22_1401_3_a_2_c: Waiver substantially contributes to administrative convenience; P_22_1401_3_a_2_d: Director may waive for groups/categories
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Tautology (Taut): Rule 18
Validation_Notes: Higher bar than individual waivers: three conjunctive conditions required. Still discretionary. HIGH-RISK implication.

Natural_Language: The head of an agency may waive any requirement in this subpart when it is determined that the contract is essential to the national security, and that its award without complying with such requirements is necessary to the national security. Upon making such a determination, the head of the agency must notify the Director of OFCCP in writing within 30 days.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1401_3_b_a: Contract essential to national security; P_22_1401_3_b_b: Award without compliance necessary to national security; P_22_1401_3_b_c: Agency head may waive; P_22_1401_3_b_d: Must notify OFCCP Director in writing within 30 days
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Tautology (Taut): Rule 18
Validation_Notes: National security waiver with mandatory notification. Waiver discretionary ("may") but 30-day OFCCP notification is mandatory if waiver granted. Both national security conditions conjunctive.

Natural_Language: The contracting officer must submit requests for waivers in accordance with agency procedures.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1401_3_c_a: CO must submit waiver requests per agency procedures
Validation_Notes: Mandatory procedural compliance for waiver requests. Simple atomic proposition.

Natural_Language: A waiver granted for a particular class of contracts may be withdrawn for any contract within that class whenever considered necessary by the Director of OFCCP to achieve the purposes of the Act. The withdrawal shall not apply to contracts awarded before the withdrawal. The withdrawal shall not apply to solicitations under any means of formal sealed bidding unless it is made more than 10 days before the date set for bid opening.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1401_3_d_a: Director may withdraw class waiver for individual contracts; P_22_1401_3_d_b: No retroactive application to awarded contracts; P_22_1401_3_d_c: No application to sealed bid solicitations unless >10 days before bid opening
Validation_Notes: Discretionary withdrawal with mandatory prospective-only application. Two temporal protections are absolute (conjunctive).

Natural_Language: Postaward requirements for Equal Opportunity for Workers with Disabilities.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1402: Parent for postaward provisions
Validation_Notes: Parent aggregating notice, CBA, complaints, and sanctions provisions.

Natural_Language: The contracting officer must furnish to the contractor appropriate notices that state the contractor's obligations and the rights of individuals with disabilities. The contracting officer may obtain these notices from the OFCCP regional office.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1402_a_a: CO must furnish disability rights/obligations notices to contractor; P_22_1402_a_b: CO may obtain notices from OFCCP regional office
Validation_Notes: Notice furnishing is mandatory; source of notices is discretionary (may obtain from OFCCP).

Natural_Language: If performance under the clause at 52.222-36 may necessitate a revision of a collective bargaining agreement, the contracting officer must advise the affected labor unions that the Department of Labor will give them appropriate opportunity to present their views. However, neither the contracting officer nor any representative shall discuss with the contractor or any labor representative any aspect of the collective bargaining agreement.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1402_b_a: Performance may necessitate CBA revision; P_22_1402_b_b: CO must advise affected unions of DOL opportunity to present views; P_22_1402_b_c: CO/representatives shall not discuss any CBA aspects with contractor or labor reps
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Negation (Neg): Rule 10
Validation_Notes: Conditional trigger (potential CBA revision) with mandatory union notification and absolute prohibition on CBA discussions. Note: prohibition on CBA discussions appears absolute regardless of trigger.

Natural_Language: Following agency procedures, the contracting office must forward any complaints received about the administration of section 503 of the Rehabilitation Act to the Director of OFCCP or any OFCCP regional or area office. OFCCP must investigate each complaint and develop a complete case record.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1402_c: Parent for complaint handling
Validation_Notes: Parent combining forwarding requirement and OFCCP investigation obligation.

Natural_Language: Following agency procedures, the contracting office must forward any complaints received about the administration of section 503 of the Rehabilitation Act of 1973, as amended (29 U.S.C. 793) to the Director of OFCCP or any OFCCP regional or area office.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1402_c_1_a: Complaints about Section 503 administration received; P_22_1402_c_1_b: Contracting office must forward per agency procedures; P_22_1402_c_1_c: Forward to OFCCP Director or regional/area office
Validation_Notes: Mandatory forwarding upon complaint receipt. Disjunctive destination (Director or regional office). HIGH-RISK implication.

Natural_Language: The OFCCP must institute investigation of each complaint and must be responsible for developing a complete case record.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1402_c_2_a: OFCCP must investigate each complaint; P_22_1402_c_2_b: OFCCP must develop complete case record
Validation_Notes: Both investigation and case record development mandatory for each complaint.

Natural_Language: The contracting officer must take necessary action, as soon as possible upon notification, to implement any sanctions imposed by DOL for violations of 52.222-36. Sanctions (per 41 CFR 60-741.66) may include withholding payments, termination or suspension of the contract, or debarment.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1402_d_a: CO receives notification of DOL sanctions; P_22_1402_d_b: CO must take action as soon as possible; P_22_1402_d_c: Sanctions may include withholding payments; P_22_1402_d_d: Sanctions may include termination/suspension; P_22_1402_d_e: Sanctions may include debarment
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Addition (Add): Rule 8
Validation_Notes: Mandatory and prompt CO action upon DOL notification. Sanction types are illustrative (may include), not exhaustive. HIGH-RISK implication.

Natural_Language: Forced or indentured child labor means all work or service exacted from any person under age 18 under menace of penalty and not voluntarily offered, or performed by any person under age 18 pursuant to a contract enforceable by process or penalties.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1501_def_fcl_a: Work/service exacted from person under 18 under menace of penalty, not voluntarily offered; P_22_1501_def_fcl_b: Work/service by person under 18 pursuant to enforceable contract
Validation_Notes: Disjunctive definition: either forced labor or indentured labor pathway. Both require person under 18.

Natural_Language: List of Products Requiring Contractor Certification as to Forced or Indentured Child Labor means the list published by DOL per EO 13126 identifying products by country of origin that DOL, Treasury, and State have reasonable basis to believe might have been mined, produced, or manufactured by forced or indentured child labor.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1501_def_list_a: Published by DOL per EO 13126; P_22_1501_def_list_b: Identifies products by country of origin; P_22_1501_def_list_c: Reasonable basis to believe products may involve forced/indentured child labor
Validation_Notes: Conjunctive definition. Three agencies involved in the reasonable basis determination. "Might have been" is lower threshold than certainty.

Natural_Language: Presolicitation requirements for prohibition of acquisition of products produced by forced or indentured child labor.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1502: Parent for presolicitation
Validation_Notes: Parent combining policy and clause/provision prescription.

Natural_Language: Agencies must take appropriate action to enforce the laws prohibiting the manufacture or importation of products mined, produced, or manufactured wholly or in part by forced or indentured child labor, consistent with 19 U.S.C. 1307, 29 U.S.C. 201, et seq., and 41 U.S.C. chapter 65. Agencies should make every effort to avoid acquiring such products.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1502_1_a: Agencies must enforce child labor prohibition laws; P_22_1502_1_b: Consistent with 19 USC 1307, 29 USC 201 et seq., 41 USC ch 65; P_22_1502_1_c: Agencies should make every effort to avoid acquiring such products
Validation_Notes: "Must" for enforcement, "should" for avoidance -- advisory element. PENDING_REVIEW due to "should" per validation rules.

Natural_Language: Solicitation provision and contract clause requirements for child labor.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1502_2: Parent for provision/clause prescriptions
Validation_Notes: Parent combining provision insertion, list checking, and trade agreement exceptions.

Natural_Language: Provision and clause prescriptions for child labor certification and cooperation.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1502_2_a: Parent for (a)(1) and (a)(2)
Validation_Notes: Parent combining certification provision and cooperation clause.

Natural_Language: Except as provided in paragraph (c), insert the provision at 52.222-18, Certification Regarding Knowledge of Child Labor for Listed End Products, in all solicitations that are expected to exceed the micro-purchase threshold and are for the acquisition of end products of a type identified by country of origin on the List. The CO must identify applicable end products and countries in paragraph (b) of 52.222-18. For solicitations >= $50,000, the CO must exclude end products from countries identified in paragraph (c) per specified thresholds.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1502_2_a_1_a: Solicitation exceeds micro-purchase threshold; P_22_1502_2_a_1_b: Acquisition of end products identified on List by country; P_22_1502_2_a_1_c: Not excepted per (c); P_22_1502_2_a_1_d: Insert provision 52.222-18; P_22_1502_2_a_1_e: CO identifies applicable products/countries in provision; P_22_1502_2_a_1_f: For >= $50K, exclude (c) countries per thresholds
Validation_Notes: Complex prescription with micro-purchase threshold trigger, List matching, trade agreement exceptions, and CO identification duties. HIGH-RISK implication.

Natural_Language: Insert the clause at 52.222-19, Child Labor -- Cooperation with Authorities and Remedies, in all solicitations and contracts for the acquisition of supplies that are expected to exceed the micro-purchase threshold.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1502_2_a_2_a: Solicitation/contract for supplies exceeds micro-purchase threshold; P_22_1502_2_a_2_b: Insert clause 52.222-19
Validation_Notes: Broader than (a)(1): applies to all supplies above MPT, not just Listed products. HIGH-RISK implication.

Natural_Language: When issuing a solicitation for supplies expected to exceed the micro-purchase threshold, the CO must check the List at www.dol.gov/ilab/. Appearance on the List is not a bar to purchase but rather an alert that there is a reasonable basis to believe the product may have been produced by forced or indentured child labor.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1502_2_b_a: Solicitation for supplies > MPT; P_22_1502_2_b_b: CO must check the List; P_22_1502_2_b_c: List appearance is alert, not bar to purchase
Validation_Notes: Mandatory List check with important clarification that listing does not prohibit purchase. Alert-based system, not ban.

Natural_Language: The requirements of this subpart resulting from List appearance do not apply if the identified country of origin is Israel (>= $50,000), Mexico (>= $102,280), or specified trade agreement countries (>= $174,000).
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1502_2_c: Parent for trade agreement exceptions
Validation_Notes: Disjunctive exceptions: any one country/threshold combination triggers exemption.

Natural_Language: Israel, and the anticipated value of the acquisition is $50,000 or more (see part 25 for the Israeli Trade Act).
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1502_2_c_1_a: Country is Israel; P_22_1502_2_c_1_b: Value >= $50,000; P_22_1502_2_c_1_c: Subpart requirements do not apply
Validation_Notes: Israeli Trade Act exception at $50K threshold. HIGH-RISK implication.

Natural_Language: Mexico, and the anticipated value of the acquisition is $102,280 or more (see part 25 for trade agreements).
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1502_2_c_2_a: Country is Mexico; P_22_1502_2_c_2_b: Value >= $102,280; P_22_1502_2_c_2_c: Subpart requirements do not apply
Validation_Notes: USMCA-related threshold. HIGH-RISK implication.

Natural_Language: Armenia, Aruba, Australia, Austria, Belgium, Bulgaria, Canada, Croatia, Cyprus, Czech Republic, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Hong Kong, Hungary, Iceland, Ireland, Italy, Japan, Korea, Latvia, Liechtenstein, Lithuania, Luxembourg, Malta, Moldova, Montenegro, Netherlands, New Zealand, North Macedonia, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Singapore, Slovak Republic, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, Taiwan, Ukraine, or the United Kingdom and the anticipated value of the acquisition is $174,000 or more.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1502_2_c_3_a: Country is listed WTO GPA/FTA partner; P_22_1502_2_c_3_b: Value >= $174,000; P_22_1502_2_c_3_c: Subpart requirements do not apply
Validation_Notes: WTO GPA and bilateral FTA partner exception at $174K threshold. Extensive country list. HIGH-RISK implication.

Natural_Language: Evaluation and award requirements for child labor provisions.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1503: Parent for evaluation/award
Validation_Notes: Parent combining certification requirements, reliance on certifications, and remedies reservation.

Natural_Language: Except as provided in (c) of 22.1502-2, before the CO may make an award for a Listed end product the offeror must certify that it will not supply Listed products from identified countries, or that it has made good faith efforts to determine whether forced/indentured child labor was used and is unaware of any such use.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1503_a: Parent for pre-award certification requirement
Validation_Notes: Disjunctive certification: offeror may certify under either pathway.

Natural_Language: The offeror certifies it will not supply any end product on the List that was mined, produced, or manufactured in a country identified on the List for that product, as specified in the solicitation.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1503_a_1_a: Offeror certifies no supply of Listed products from identified countries
Validation_Notes: Clean certification: absolute commitment not to supply from identified countries.

Natural_Language: The offeror certifies it has made a good faith effort to determine whether forced or indentured child labor was used, and on the basis of those efforts, the offeror is unaware of any such use.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1503_a_2_a: Good faith effort to determine child labor use; P_22_1503_a_2_b: Unaware of any such use based on those efforts
Validation_Notes: Due diligence certification: both effort and unawareness required. Lower bar than (a)(1) absolute commitment.

Natural_Language: Absent any actual knowledge that the certification is false, the contracting officer must rely on the offerors' certifications in making award decisions.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1503_b_a: CO has no actual knowledge certification is false; P_22_1503_b_b: CO must rely on offeror certifications for award
Validation_Notes: Absent-knowledge condition triggers mandatory reliance. "Actual knowledge" is high bar -- constructive knowledge insufficient. HIGH-RISK implication.

Natural_Language: Proper certification will not prevent the head of an agency from imposing remedies in accordance with 22.1504 if it is later discovered that the contractor has furnished an end product or component that has in fact been mined, produced, or manufactured, wholly or in part, using forced or indentured child labor.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1503_c_a: Proper certification was provided; P_22_1503_c_b: Later discovery of actual child labor use; P_22_1503_c_c: Agency head may still impose remedies per 22.1504
Validation_Notes: Certification is not a shield against post-discovery remedies. Preserves government enforcement authority despite prior certification. HIGH-RISK implication.

Natural_Language: Postaward requirements for child labor violations.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1504: Parent for postaward enforcement
Validation_Notes: Parent combining investigation referral, violation categories, and remedy types.

Natural_Language: Whenever a CO has reason to believe that forced or indentured child labor was used to mine, produce, or manufacture an end product furnished pursuant to a contract subject to certification, the CO must refer the matter for investigation by the agency IG, Attorney General, or Secretary of the Treasury per agency procedures, except for products from countries listed in 22.1502-2(c) under contracts exceeding applicable thresholds.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1504_a_a: CO has reason to believe child labor used; P_22_1504_a_b: End product furnished under certified contract; P_22_1504_a_c: Not excepted per 22.1502-2(c) thresholds; P_22_1504_a_d: CO must refer for investigation to IG/AG/Treasury Secretary per agency procedures
Validation_Notes: Mandatory referral upon reasonable belief. Three possible investigative recipients (disjunctive per agency procedures). Trade agreement exception preserved.

Natural_Language: The Government may impose remedies for the following violations: false certification, failure to cooperate with investigation per 52.222-19, use of forced/indentured child labor in processes, or furnishing products made with such labor. Remedies for (b)(2) and (b)(3) inappropriate unless contractor knew of violation.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1504_b: Parent for violation categories
Validation_Notes: Disjunctive violation categories: any single violation type can trigger remedies.

Natural_Language: The contractor has submitted a false certification regarding knowledge of the use of forced or indentured child labor.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1504_b_1_a: False certification submitted regarding child labor knowledge
Validation_Notes: False certification violation. No knowledge qualifier -- strict liability for false cert.

Natural_Language: The contractor has failed to cooperate as required in accordance with the clause at 52.222-19 with an investigation of the use of forced or indentured child labor.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1504_b_2_a: Contractor failed to cooperate with investigation per 52.222-19
Validation_Notes: Cooperation failure violation. Note: remedies per source text inappropriate unless contractor knew.

Natural_Language: The contractor uses forced or indentured child labor in its mining, production, or manufacturing processes.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1504_b_3_a: Contractor uses forced/indentured child labor in its own processes
Validation_Notes: Direct use violation. Note: remedies per source text inappropriate unless contractor knew.

Natural_Language: The contractor has furnished an end product or component mined, produced, or manufactured, wholly or in part, by forced or indentured child labor. Remedies in paragraphs (b)(2) and (b)(3) are inappropriate unless the contractor knew of the violation.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1504_b_4_a: Contractor furnished product made with child labor; P_22_1504_b_4_b: Knowledge qualifier for (b)(2)/(b)(3) remedies
Validation_Notes: Product-level violation. Importantly, knowledge qualifier applies to (b)(2) and (b)(3) remedies, not to (b)(4) itself.

Natural_Language: The Government may impose the following remedies: contract termination by CO, suspension by S&D official per subpart 9.4, or debarment for up to 3 years by S&D official per subpart 9.4.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1504_c: Parent for available remedies
Validation_Notes: Disjunctive remedies: any one or combination may be imposed.

Natural_Language: The contracting officer may terminate the contract.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1504_c_1_a: CO may terminate contract
Validation_Notes: Discretionary remedy. Tautology for "may."

Natural_Language: The suspending and debarring official may suspend the contractor in accordance with the procedures in subpart 9.4.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1504_c_2_a: S&D official may suspend per subpart 9.4
Validation_Notes: Discretionary suspension remedy. Must follow subpart 9.4 procedures.

Natural_Language: The suspending and debarring official may debar the contractor for a period not to exceed 3 years in accordance with the procedures in subpart 9.4.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1504_c_3_a: S&D official may debar for up to 3 years per subpart 9.4
Validation_Notes: Discretionary debarment with 3-year cap. Must follow subpart 9.4 procedures.

Natural_Language: United States, as used in this subpart, means the 50 States, the District of Columbia, Puerto Rico, the Commonwealth of the Northern Mariana Islands, American Samoa, Guam, the U.S. Virgin Islands, and Wake Island.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1601_def_US_16_a: US for Subpart 22.16 includes 50 States, DC, PR, CNMI, American Samoa, Guam, USVI, and Wake Island
Validation_Notes: Subpart-specific US definition. Broader than Subpart 22.17 (which excludes territories except outlying areas) but narrower than Subpart 22.19 (which includes OCS).

Natural_Language: Presolicitation requirements for NLRA employee rights notification.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1602: Parent for presolicitation
Validation_Notes: Parent combining policy and clause prescription.

Natural_Language: Policy for NLRA notification requirements under EO 13496.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1602_1: Parent for policy provisions
Validation_Notes: Parent aggregating EO implementation, notice content, exceptions, and exemption authority.

Natural_Language: This subpart prescribes policies and procedures to implement Executive Order 13496, dated January 30, 2009. EO 13496 requires contractors to post a notice informing employees of their rights under Federal labor laws.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1602_1_a_a: Subpart implements EO 13496; P_22_1602_1_a_b: Contractors must post employee rights notice
Validation_Notes: Scope-setting provision establishing EO authority and core posting requirement.

Natural_Language: The Secretary has determined that the notice must contain employee rights under the National Labor Relations Act (29 U.S.C. 151 et seq.). The Act encourages collective bargaining, and protects the exercise by employees of their freedom to associate, self-organize, and designate representatives for negotiating terms and conditions of employment.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1602_1_b_a: Notice must contain NLRA rights per Secretary determination; P_22_1602_1_b_b: NLRA covers collective bargaining, association, self-organization, representative designation
Validation_Notes: Secretary-determined notice content. Descriptive of NLRA scope.

Natural_Language: The requirements of this subpart do not apply to contracts under the simplified acquisition threshold, subcontracts of $10,000 or less, or contracts/subcontracts for work performed exclusively outside the United States.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1602_1_c: Parent for exceptions
Validation_Notes: Disjunctive exceptions: any one triggers non-applicability.

Natural_Language: Contracts under the simplified acquisition threshold.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1602_1_c_1_a: Contract under SAT; P_22_1602_1_c_1_b: Subpart does not apply
Validation_Notes: SAT exception. HIGH-RISK implication.

Natural_Language: Subcontracts of $10,000 or less.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1602_1_c_2_a: Subcontract <= $10,000; P_22_1602_1_c_2_b: Subpart does not apply
Validation_Notes: $10K subcontract threshold. HIGH-RISK implication.

Natural_Language: Contracts or subcontracts for work performed exclusively outside the United States.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1602_1_c_3_a: Work performed exclusively outside US; P_22_1602_1_c_3_b: Subpart does not apply
Validation_Notes: Geographic exception. "Exclusively" is key qualifier. HIGH-RISK implication.

Natural_Language: The Secretary may exempt departments/agencies from requirements if they impair economical/efficient procurement or if special circumstances require exemption in the national interest. Exemptions may cover particular contracts/subcontracts or classes thereof, including the requirement to include clause 52.222-40. Requests per 29 CFR 471.3.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1602_1_d: Parent for Secretary exemption authority
Validation_Notes: Parent combining exemption authority and request procedures.

Natural_Language: If the Secretary finds that the requirements of the Executive Order impair the ability of the Government to procure goods and services on an economical and efficient basis or if special circumstances require an exemption in order to serve the national interest, the Secretary may exempt a contracting department or agency, or groups of departments or agencies, from the requirements of any or all of the provisions of this Executive Order with respect to a particular contract or subcontract, or any class of contracts or subcontracts, including the requirement to include the clause at 52.222-40.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1602_1_d_1_a: Requirements impair economical/efficient procurement; P_22_1602_1_d_1_b: Special circumstances require exemption for national interest; P_22_1602_1_d_1_c: Secretary may exempt departments/agencies; P_22_1602_1_d_1_d: Exemption may cover individual or class of contracts
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Addition (Add): Rule 8; Tautology (Taut): Rule 18; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7
Validation_Notes: Disjunctive trigger (impairment or national interest), discretionary exemption (may). Broad scope covering individual or class exemptions. HIGH-RISK implication.

Natural_Language: Requests for exemptions may be submitted in accordance with Department of Labor regulations at 29 CFR 471.3.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1602_1_d_2_a: Exemption requests per 29 CFR 471.3
Validation_Notes: Procedural cross-reference for exemption requests.

Natural_Language: Contract clause requirements for NLRA notification.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1602_2: Parent for clause prescription
Validation_Notes: Parent combining clause insertion and modification authority.

Natural_Language: Insert the clause at 52.222-40, Notification of Employee Rights under the NLRA, in all solicitations and contracts, including commercial products, commercial services, and COTS items, except acquisitions under the SAT (for IDIQs, include only if annual order value expected to exceed SAT), for work performed exclusively outside US, or covered entirely by Secretary exemption.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1602_2_a_a: All solicitations and contracts including commercial; P_22_1602_2_a_b: Not under SAT (IDIQ: annual order value > SAT); P_22_1602_2_a_c: Not exclusively outside US; P_22_1602_2_a_d: Not fully exempted by Secretary; P_22_1602_2_a_e: Insert clause 52.222-40
Validation_Notes: Broad clause prescription covering commercial acquisitions. Three exceptions mirror 22.1602-1(c). IDIQ special rule for SAT threshold. HIGH-RISK implication.

Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1602_2_b_a: Secretary exemption granted; P_22_1602_2_b_b: Agency may modify clause to reflect exemption
Validation_Notes: Discretionary clause modification upon exemption. Tautology for "may."

Natural_Language: Postaward requirements for NLRA notification.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1603: Parent for postaward provisions
Validation_Notes: Parent aggregating compliance evaluation, cooperation, Secretary actions, and enforcement limitations.

Validation_Notes: Discretionary enforcement authority (may) with disjunctive methods and conjunctive purpose.

Validation_Notes: Mandatory interagency cooperation. Scope of cooperation defined by Secretary requirements.

Validation_Notes: Violation determination triggers discretionary enforcement. Specific actions cross-referenced to CFR. HIGH-RISK implication.

Natural_Language: The Secretary may not terminate or suspend a contract or suspend or debar a contractor if the agency head has provided written objections including a statement of reasons and finding that contractor performance is essential to the agency mission, and continues to object. Procedures for enforcement at 29 CFR 471.10 through 471.16.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1603_d_a: Agency head provides written objections with reasons; P_22_1603_d_b: Finding that performance essential to agency mission; P_22_1603_d_c: Agency head continues to object; P_22_1603_d_d: Secretary may not terminate/suspend contract or suspend/debar contractor
Validation_Notes: Agency head override of Secretary enforcement. All three conditions conjunctive. Significant interagency power dynamic -- agency mission trumps labor enforcement when agency head objects. HIGH-RISK implication.

Natural_Language: This subpart prescribes policy for implementing 22 U.S.C. chapter 78 and Executive Order 13627, Strengthening Protections Against Trafficking in Persons in Federal Contracts, dated September 25, 2012.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1700_a: Subpart implements 22 USC ch 78; P_22_1700_b: Subpart implements EO 13627
Validation_Notes: Dual authority: statute and executive order. Scope-setting provision.

Natural_Language: Applicability of Subpart 22.17.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1701: Parent for applicability
Validation_Notes: Parent combining universal applicability and certification threshold.

Natural_Language: This subpart applies to all acquisitions.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1701_a_a: Subpart applies to all acquisitions without exception
Validation_Notes: Universal applicability: no dollar threshold, no type exception. One of the broadest FAR applicability statements.

Natural_Language: The requirement at 22.1703-1(b) for a certification and compliance plan applies only to any portion of a contract or subcontract that is for supplies (other than COTS) to be acquired outside the US, or services to be performed outside the US, and has an estimated value that exceeds $550,000.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1701_b_a: Contract/subcontract portion for non-COTS supplies outside US or services outside US; P_22_1701_b_b: Estimated value exceeds $550,000; P_22_1701_b_c: Certification/compliance plan requirement per 22.1703-1(b) applies
Validation_Notes: Narrower applicability for certification requirement vs. universal clause applicability in (a). Both conditions conjunctive. HIGH-RISK implication.

Natural_Language: Agent means any individual, including a director, an officer, an employee, or an independent contractor, authorized to act on behalf of the organization.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1702_def_agent_a: Individual authorized to act on behalf of organization; P_22_1702_def_agent_b: Includes directors, officers, employees, independent contractors
Validation_Notes: Broad definitional scope -- includes ICs. Authorization is the key element.

Natural_Language: Coercion means threats of serious harm to or physical restraint against any person; any scheme/plan/pattern intended to cause belief that failure to act would result in serious harm or restraint; or abuse or threatened abuse of the legal process.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1702_def_coercion_a: Threats of serious harm or physical restraint; P_22_1702_def_coercion_b: Scheme/plan/pattern to cause belief of harm for non-performance; P_22_1702_def_coercion_c: Abuse or threatened abuse of legal process
Validation_Notes: Tripartite disjunctive definition: any single pathway constitutes coercion.

Natural_Language: Commercial sex act means any sex act on account of which anything of value is given to or received by any person.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1702_def_csa_a: Sex act occurs; P_22_1702_def_csa_b: Anything of value given to or received by any person on account of act
Validation_Notes: Conjunctive: both the act and the value exchange required. Broad "anything of value" standard.

Natural_Language: Debt bondage means the status or condition arising from a pledge of personal services as security for debt, if the value of services as reasonably assessed is not applied toward debt liquidation or the length/nature of services are not limited and defined.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1702_def_db_a: Pledge of personal services as debt security; P_22_1702_def_db_b: Value not applied toward debt liquidation; P_22_1702_def_db_c: Length/nature of services not limited and defined
Justification_Rules: Biconditional (Bicond): Rule 17; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Addition (Add): Rule 8
Validation_Notes: Pledge is required (conjunctive), then either exploitation pathway triggers (disjunctive).

Natural_Language: Employee means an employee of the Contractor directly engaged in the performance of work under the contract who has other than a minimal impact or involvement in contract performance.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1702_def_employee_a: Employee of contractor; P_22_1702_def_employee_b: Directly engaged in contract work; P_22_1702_def_employee_c: More than minimal impact/involvement
Validation_Notes: Three conjunctive conditions. "Other than minimal" excludes truly incidental involvement.

Natural_Language: Forced labor means knowingly providing or obtaining the labor or services of a person by threats of serious harm or physical restraint; by scheme/plan/pattern to cause belief of serious harm; or by abuse or threatened abuse of law or legal process.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1702_def_fl_a: Knowingly providing/obtaining labor; P_22_1702_def_fl_b: By threats of serious harm/restraint; P_22_1702_def_fl_c: By scheme causing belief of harm; P_22_1702_def_fl_d: By abuse of law/legal process
Justification_Rules: Biconditional (Bicond): Rule 17; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Addition (Add): Rule 8
Validation_Notes: "Knowingly" is required element (conjunctive). Method is tripartite disjunctive, mirroring coercion definition structure.

Natural_Language: Involuntary servitude includes a condition of servitude induced by scheme/plan/pattern to cause belief of serious harm or restraint, or by abuse or threatened abuse of the legal process.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1702_def_is_a: Scheme/plan/pattern causing belief of harm if not continuing; P_22_1702_def_is_b: Abuse or threatened abuse of legal process
Validation_Notes: Disjunctive definition. "Includes" suggests non-exhaustive but these are the enumerated methods. Narrower than forced labor (no direct threats pathway).

Natural_Language: Recruitment fees means fees of any type, including charges, costs, assessments, or other financial obligations, that are associated with the recruiting process, regardless of time, manner, or location of imposition or collection. Includes extensive enumerated categories in (1) and applies regardless of payment method per (2).
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1702_def_rf_a: Fees of any type associated with recruiting process; P_22_1702_def_rf_b: Regardless of time/manner/location of imposition; P_22_1702_def_rf_c: Includes enumerated categories per (1); P_22_1702_def_rf_d: Applies regardless of payment method per (2)
Validation_Notes: Extremely broad definition. "Any type" and "regardless of" language eliminates common avoidance strategies. 13 enumerated fee categories in (1) and 5 payment methods in (2) are illustrative, not exhaustive.

Natural_Language: Severe forms of trafficking in persons means (1) Sex trafficking in which a commercial sex act is induced by force, fraud, or coercion, or in which the person induced to perform such act has not attained 18 years of age; or (2) The recruitment, harboring, transportation, provision, or obtaining of a person for labor or services, through the use of force, fraud, or coercion for the purpose of subjection to involuntary servitude, peonage, debt bondage, or slavery.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1702_def_severe_a: Sex trafficking induced by force, fraud, or coercion, or involving person under 18; P_22_1702_def_severe_b: Recruitment/harboring/transportation/provision/obtaining of person for labor through force/fraud/coercion for involuntary servitude/peonage/debt bondage/slavery
Validation_Notes: Definitional biconditional with disjunctive structure. Either pathway constitutes severe trafficking. Logically sound and regulatory-sensible.

Natural_Language: Sex trafficking means the recruitment, harboring, transportation, provision, obtaining, patronizing, or soliciting of a person for the purpose of a commercial sex act.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1702_def_sex_trafficking_a: Activity is recruitment/harboring/transportation/provision/obtaining/patronizing/soliciting of a person; P_22_1702_def_sex_trafficking_b: Purpose is a commercial sex act
Validation_Notes: Both elements required: the activity AND the purpose. Conjunctive definition with biconditional frame.

Natural_Language: Subcontractor means any supplier, distributor, vendor, or firm that furnishes supplies or services to or for a prime contractor or another subcontractor.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1702_def_subcontractor_a: Entity is supplier/distributor/vendor/firm; P_22_1702_def_subcontractor_b: Furnishes supplies or services to/for a prime contractor or another subcontractor
Validation_Notes: Standard definitional biconditional. Both entity type and activity required.

Natural_Language: United States means the 50 States, the District of Columbia, and outlying areas.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1702_def_US_17_a: United States as defined for Subpart 22.17 includes 50 States, DC, and outlying areas
Validation_Notes: Simple definitional. Note: narrower definition than some other subparts (compare 22.1901 which includes territories).

Natural_Language: Presolicitation requirements for combating trafficking in persons.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1703: Parent proposition for presolicitation requirements under Subpart 22.17
Validation_Notes: Parent aggregating requirements (22.1703-1) and clause prescriptions (22.1703-2).

Natural_Language: Requirements for Government solicitations and contracts regarding combating trafficking in persons, including prohibitions and compliance plan requirements.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1703_1: Parent for trafficking presolicitation requirements
Validation_Notes: Parent combining general prohibitions (a) and certification/compliance plan requirements (b).

Natural_Language: The United States Government has adopted a policy prohibiting trafficking in persons. Government solicitations and contracts must prohibit trafficking activities, require notifications, require disclosures and cooperation, and provide remedies.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1703_1_a: Parent for general trafficking prohibition requirements
Validation_Notes: All four requirements mandatory for government solicitations and contracts.

Natural_Language: Government solicitations and contracts must prohibit contractors, contractor employees, subcontractors, subcontractor employees, and their agents from the trafficking-related activities listed in paragraph (b) of the clause at 52.222-50, Combating Trafficking in Persons.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1703_1_a_1_a: Solicitations and contracts must contain prohibition; P_22_1703_1_a_1_b: Prohibition covers contractors/employees/subcontractors/agents; P_22_1703_1_a_1_c: Prohibited activities are those listed in 52.222-50(b)
Validation_Notes: Mandatory prohibition. Cross-references 52.222-50(b) for the specific prohibited activities.

Natural_Language: Government solicitations and contracts must require contractors and subcontractors to notify employees of the prohibited activities referenced in paragraph (a)(1) and the actions that may be taken against them for violations.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1703_1_a_2_a: Contractors/subcontractors must notify employees of prohibited activities; P_22_1703_1_a_2_b: Notification must include potential actions for violations
Validation_Notes: Notification requirement depends on the prohibitions in (a)(1).

Natural_Language: Government solicitations and contracts must require the contractor and subcontractors to disclose violations, provide documents, and cooperate with audits and investigations.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1703_1_a_3: Parent for disclosure/cooperation requirements
Validation_Notes: All three sub-requirements are mandatory.

Natural_Language: Require the contractor and subcontractors to disclose to the contracting officer and the agency Inspector General information sufficient to identify the nature and extent of an offense and the individuals responsible for the conduct.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1703_1_a_3_i_a: Disclosure to CO and agency IG required; P_22_1703_1_a_3_i_b: Information must be sufficient to identify nature/extent of offense and responsible individuals
Validation_Notes: Mandatory disclosure with specificity requirements.

Natural_Language: Require the contractor and subcontractors to provide timely and complete responses to Government auditors' and investigators' requests for documents.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1703_1_a_3_ii_a: Responses to auditors/investigators must be timely; P_22_1703_1_a_3_ii_b: Responses must be complete
Validation_Notes: Both timeliness and completeness are required for document responses.

Natural_Language: Require the contractor and subcontractors to cooperate fully in providing reasonable access to their facilities and staff (both inside and outside the U.S.) to allow contracting agencies and other responsible Federal agencies to conduct audits, investigations, or other actions to ascertain compliance with the Trafficking Victims Protection Act (22 U.S.C. chapter 78), Executive Order 13627, or any other applicable law or regulation.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1703_1_a_3_iii_a: Full cooperation required; P_22_1703_1_a_3_iii_b: Reasonable access to facilities and staff inside and outside US; P_22_1703_1_a_3_iii_c: Purpose is compliance ascertainment under TVPA, EO 13627, or other applicable law
Validation_Notes: Comprehensive cooperation requirement extending to overseas facilities.

Natural_Language: Government solicitations and contracts must provide suitable remedies, including termination, to be imposed on contractors that fail to comply with the requirements of paragraphs (a)(1) through (3) and (b).
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1703_1_a_4_a: Suitable remedies must be provided; P_22_1703_1_a_4_b: Remedies include termination; P_22_1703_1_a_4_c: Remedies apply to noncompliant contractors
Validation_Notes: Noncompliance triggers remedy provision. Uses HIGH-RISK implication. Termination explicitly included but not exclusively required -- "including" signals non-exhaustive list.

Natural_Language: With regard to certification and a compliance plan, Government solicitations and contracts must meet requirements for pre-award certification, annual certifications, subcontractor certifications, subcontractor annual certifications, and plan proportionality.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1703_1_b: Parent for certification and compliance plan requirements
Validation_Notes: All five certification/compliance sub-requirements are mandatory.

Natural_Language: Require the apparent successful offeror to provide, before contract award, a certification (see 52.222-56) that the offeror has a compliance plan if any portion of the contract or subcontract is for supplies (other than COTS) acquired outside the US or services performed outside the US, and the estimated value exceeds $550,000.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1703_1_b_1_a: Portion of contract/subcontract is for non-COTS supplies acquired outside US or services performed outside US; P_22_1703_1_b_1_b: Estimated value exceeds $550,000; P_22_1703_1_b_1_c: Pre-award certification required per 52.222-56
Validation_Notes: Conditional trigger: both non-COTS outside US AND >$550K threshold must be met. HIGH-RISK implication used. Cross-references 52.222-56 and COTS definition at 2.101.

Natural_Language: The certification must state that the offeror has implemented the plan and procedures to prevent prohibited activities and to monitor/detect/terminate, and that after due diligence either no agents/subcontractors have engaged in prohibited activities, or appropriate remedial and referral actions have been taken.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1703_1_b_1_ii_A: Plan implemented with prevention/monitoring/detection/termination procedures; P_22_1703_1_b_1_ii_B1: No engagement in prohibited activities after due diligence; P_22_1703_1_b_1_ii_B2: If abuses found, appropriate remedial and referral actions taken
Validation_Notes: Plan implementation is mandatory (conjunctive), while due diligence outcome is disjunctive -- either clean or remediated.

Natural_Language: Require annual certifications (see 52.222-50(h)(5)) during performance of the contract, when a compliance plan was required at award.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1703_1_b_2_a: Compliance plan was required at award; P_22_1703_1_b_2_b: Annual certifications required during performance
Validation_Notes: Conditional: annual certs only when compliance plan was required at award. HIGH-RISK implication.

Natural_Language: Require the contractor to obtain a certification from each subcontractor, prior to subcontract award, if any portion of the subcontract is for non-COTS supplies acquired outside US or services performed outside US, and the estimated value exceeds $550,000. Certification must state subcontractor has implemented compliance plan and either no prohibited activities found or remedial actions taken.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1703_1_b_3_a: Subcontract portion for non-COTS outside US; P_22_1703_1_b_3_b: Estimated value exceeds $550,000; P_22_1703_1_b_3_c: Pre-award subcontractor certification required; P_22_1703_1_b_3_d: Certification states compliance plan implemented and due diligence results
Validation_Notes: Mirrors prime contractor certification threshold and content requirements at subcontractor level. Same $550K/non-COTS/outside-US trigger.

Natural_Language: Require the contractor to obtain annual certifications from subcontractors during performance of the contract, when a compliance plan was required at the time of subcontract award.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1703_1_b_4_a: Compliance plan required at subcontract award; P_22_1703_1_b_4_b: Annual subcontractor certifications required during performance
Validation_Notes: Parallels (b)(2) annual cert requirement at subcontractor level.

Natural_Language: Require that any compliance plan or procedures must be appropriate to the size and complexity of the contract and the nature and scope of its activities, including the number of non-U.S. citizens expected to be employed and the risk that the contract or subcontract will involve services or supplies susceptible to trafficking in persons. The minimum elements of the plan are specified at 52.222-50(h).
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1703_1_b_5_a: Plan must be appropriate to contract size/complexity; P_22_1703_1_b_5_b: Plan must be appropriate to nature/scope of activities; P_22_1703_1_b_5_c: Considerations include number of non-US citizens and trafficking susceptibility risk; P_22_1703_1_b_5_d: Minimum elements per 52.222-50(h)
Validation_Notes: Proportionality requirement -- plan scales to contract characteristics. All elements conjunctive.

Natural_Language: Solicitation provisions and contract clauses for combating trafficking in persons.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1703_2: Parent for clause prescription requirements
Validation_Notes: Parent aggregating clause (a) and provision (b) prescriptions.

Natural_Language: Clause prescriptions for 52.222-50, Combating Trafficking in Persons.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1703_2_a: Parent for 52.222-50 clause prescription
Validation_Notes: Parent for base clause and alternate usage.

Natural_Language: Insert the clause at 52.222-50, Combating Trafficking in Persons, in all solicitations and contracts.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1703_2_a_1_a: Clause 52.222-50 required in all solicitations and contracts
Validation_Notes: Universal applicability -- no threshold or exception. All solicitations and contracts.

Natural_Language: Use the clause with its Alternate I when the contract will be performed outside the United States and the contracting officer has been notified of specific U.S. directives or notices regarding combating trafficking in persons that apply to contractor employees at the contract place of performance.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1703_2_a_2_a: Contract performed outside US; P_22_1703_2_a_2_b: CO notified of specific US directives/notices re trafficking; P_22_1703_2_a_2_c: Use Alternate I of 52.222-50
Validation_Notes: Both conditions must be met: outside-US performance AND CO notification of specific directives. HIGH-RISK implication.

Natural_Language: Insert the provision at 52.222-56, Certification Regarding Trafficking in Persons Compliance Plan, in solicitations if it is possible that at least $550,000 of the value of the contract may be performed outside the United States and the acquisition is not entirely for commercially available off-the-shelf items.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1703_2_b_1: Possible that >= $550K performed outside US; P_22_1703_2_b_2: Acquisition not entirely for COTS items; P_22_1703_2_b_3: Insert provision 52.222-56
Validation_Notes: Dual condition trigger for provision insertion. Note "possible" language -- lower threshold than certainty. HIGH-RISK implication.

Natural_Language: Postaward requirements for combating trafficking in persons.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1704: Parent for postaward trafficking requirements
Validation_Notes: Parent aggregating violations definition, credible information response, IG report handling, and remedies.

Natural_Language: It is a violation of the Trafficking Victims Protection Act of 2000, as amended, (22 U.S.C. chapter 78), E.O. 13627, or the policies of this subpart if the contractor, contractor employee, subcontractor, subcontractor employee, or agent fails to comply with the requirements of the clause at 52.222-50, Combating Trafficking in Persons.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1704_a_a: Entity is contractor/employee/subcontractor/employee/agent; P_22_1704_a_b: Entity fails to comply with 52.222-50; P_22_1704_a_c: Failure constitutes violation of TVPA/EO 13627/subpart policies
Validation_Notes: Establishes that noncompliance by covered entities equals a statutory/executive order violation. HIGH-RISK implication.

Natural_Language: Upon receipt of credible information regarding a violation listed in paragraph (a), the contracting officer must promptly notify the agency Inspector General, the agency debarring and suspending official, and if appropriate, law enforcement officials; and may direct the contractor to take specific steps to abate the alleged violation or enforce the requirements of its compliance plan.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1704_b_a: CO receives credible information of violation per (a); P_22_1704_b_b: CO must promptly notify agency IG; P_22_1704_b_c: CO must notify debarring/suspending official; P_22_1704_b_d: CO must notify law enforcement if appropriate; P_22_1704_b_e: CO may direct contractor to abate violation or enforce compliance plan
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Tautology (Taut): Rule 18
Validation_Notes: Mandatory notifications (must) plus discretionary direction (may). Law enforcement notification qualified by "if appropriate." Tautology used for may/discretion.

Natural_Language: Receipt of agency Inspector General report: the head of executive agency must ensure CO receives copy of IG report. Upon receipt of report supporting allegations, head must refer to suspending/debarring official and delegate authority for administrative proceeding.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1704_c: Parent for IG report handling
Validation_Notes: Parent combining CO notification requirement and substantiation process.

Natural_Language: The head of an executive agency must ensure that the contracting officer is provided a copy of the agency Inspector General report of an investigation of a violation of the trafficking in persons prohibitions in 52.222-50(b).
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1704_c_1_a: IG report exists for trafficking violation investigation; P_22_1704_c_1_b: Agency head must ensure CO receives copy
Validation_Notes: Mandatory notification chain from IG through agency head to CO. HIGH-RISK implication.

Natural_Language: Upon receipt of a report from the agency Inspector General that provides support for the allegations, the head of the executive agency must refer the matter to the agency suspending and debarring official and delegate to an authorized official the responsibility to expeditiously conduct an administrative proceeding, make a final determination, and notify the CO.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1704_c_2_a: IG report supports allegations; P_22_1704_c_2_b: Agency head must refer to S&D official; P_22_1704_c_2_c: Agency head must delegate administrative proceeding authority; P_22_1704_c_2_d: Proceeding must allow contractor opportunity to respond; P_22_1704_c_2_e: Final determination required; P_22_1704_c_2_f: CO must be notified of determination
Validation_Notes: Complex mandatory chain triggered by IG report supporting allegations. All subsequent actions are conjunctive (all required). Due process element in allowing contractor response.

Natural_Language: The suspending and debarring official has the authority, at any time before or after the final determination, to use the suspension and debarment procedures in subpart 9.4 to suspend, propose for debarment, or debar the contractor, if appropriate, also considering the factors in paragraph (d)(2).
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1704_c_2_ii_a: S&D official has authority at any time; P_22_1704_c_2_ii_b: May use subpart 9.4 procedures; P_22_1704_c_2_ii_c: Actions include suspend/propose debarment/debar; P_22_1704_c_2_ii_d: Must consider factors in (d)(2)
Validation_Notes: Discretionary authority ("if appropriate") modeled as tautology. Cross-references subpart 9.4 and (d)(2) factors. Timing is unrestricted (before or after final determination).

Natural_Language: After a final determination that the allegations of a trafficking in persons violation are substantiated, the contracting officer must enter the violation in FAPIIS and consider taking any of the remedies specified in 52.222-50(e).
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1704_d: Parent for remedies after substantiated violation
Validation_Notes: Parent combining FAPIIS entry requirement and remedies consideration.

Natural_Language: Enter the violation in FAPIIS (see part 42).
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1704_d_1_a: Substantiated violation exists; P_22_1704_d_1_b: CO must enter violation in FAPIIS
Validation_Notes: Mandatory FAPIIS entry upon substantiation. Cross-references Part 42.

Natural_Language: Consider taking any of the remedies specified in paragraph (e) of the clause at 52.222-50, Combating Trafficking in Persons. These remedies are in addition to any other remedies available to the United States Government.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1704_d_2_a: CO must consider remedies in 52.222-50(e); P_22_1704_d_2_b: Remedies are in addition to other available Government remedies
Validation_Notes: "Consider" is mandatory (must consider) but actual remedy selection is discretionary. Non-exclusive remedies.

Natural_Language: Commercially available off-the-shelf (COTS) item means any item of supply that is a commercial product (as defined in paragraph (1) of the definition at 2.101), sold in substantial quantities in the commercial marketplace, and offered to the Government without modification in the same form sold commercially. Does not include bulk cargo.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1801_def_COTS_a: Item is commercial product per 2.101(1); P_22_1801_def_COTS_b: Sold in substantial quantities commercially; P_22_1801_def_COTS_c: Offered to Government without modification; P_22_1801_def_COTS_d: Not bulk cargo per 46 USC 40102(4)
Justification_Rules: Biconditional (Bicond): Rule 17; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Negation (Neg): Rule 10
Validation_Notes: Conjunctive definition with negation of bulk cargo exclusion. All positive elements plus exclusion required.

Natural_Language: Employee assigned to the contract means an employee who was hired after November 6, 1986 (after November 27, 2009, in CNMI), who is directly performing work in the United States under a contract required to include 52.222-54. Not considered directly performing if employee normally performs support/indirect work and does not perform any substantial duties applicable to the contract.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1801_def_ea_a: Hired after Nov 6 1986 (Nov 27 2009 in CNMI); P_22_1801_def_ea_b: Directly performing work in US under contract with 52.222-54; P_22_1801_def_ea_c: Not if normally performs support/indirect functions; P_22_1801_def_ea_d: Not if no substantial duties applicable to contract
Justification_Rules: Biconditional (Bicond): Rule 17; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Negation (Neg): Rule 10
Validation_Notes: Complex definition with affirmative requirements and conjunctive exclusion. Both exclusion conditions must be met to negate assignment status. CNMI date exception noted.

Natural_Language: Subcontract means any contract, as defined in 2.101, entered into by a subcontractor to furnish supplies or services for performance of a prime contract or a subcontract. Includes purchase orders and changes/modifications to purchase orders.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1801_def_subcontract_18_a: Contract per 2.101 entered by subcontractor; P_22_1801_def_subcontract_18_b: Purpose is to furnish supplies/services for prime or subcontract performance; P_22_1801_def_subcontract_18_c: Includes POs and PO modifications
Validation_Notes: Standard definitional biconditional. Explicitly includes POs.

Natural_Language: Subcontractor means any supplier, distributor, vendor, or firm that furnishes supplies or services to or for a prime contractor or another subcontractor.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1801_def_subcontractor_18_a: Entity is supplier/distributor/vendor/firm; P_22_1801_def_subcontractor_18_b: Furnishes supplies/services to/for prime contractor or another subcontractor
Validation_Notes: Identical to Subpart 22.17 definition. Standard definitional biconditional.

Natural_Language: United States means the 50 States, the District of Columbia, Puerto Rico, Guam, the Commonwealth of the Northern Mariana Islands and the U.S. Virgin Islands, as defined in 8 U.S.C. 1101(a)(38).
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1801_def_US_18_a: US for Subpart 22.18 includes 50 States, DC, PR, Guam, CNMI, USVI per 8 USC 1101(a)(38)
Validation_Notes: Broader than Subpart 22.17 definition (includes territories). Per immigration statute definition.

Natural_Language: Presolicitation requirements for Employment Eligibility Verification.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1802: Parent for E-Verify presolicitation requirements
Validation_Notes: Parent combining policy (22.1802-1) and clause (22.1802-2).

Natural_Language: Policy for E-Verify employment eligibility verification requirements.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1802_1: Parent for E-Verify policy provisions
Validation_Notes: Parent aggregating all E-Verify policy sub-provisions (a) through (f).

Natural_Language: This subpart prescribes policies and procedures requiring contractors to utilize the DHS USCIS employment eligibility verification program (E-Verify) as the means for verifying employment eligibility of certain employees.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1802_1_a_a: Subpart requires contractor use of E-Verify; P_22_1802_1_a_b: E-Verify is DHS USCIS program; P_22_1802_1_a_c: Applies to certain employees
Validation_Notes: Scope-setting provision establishing E-Verify as the required verification method.

Natural_Language: Statutes and Executive orders require employers to abide by the immigration laws of the United States and to employ in the United States only individuals who are eligible to work. E-Verify provides an Internet-based means of verifying employment eligibility but is not a substitute for any other employment eligibility verification requirements.

Validation_Notes: Important policy clarification: E-Verify supplements but does not replace other requirements.

Natural_Language: Contracting officers must include in solicitations and contracts requirements that Federal contractors must enroll in E-Verify, use E-Verify for new hires, use E-Verify for employees assigned to the contract, and include these requirements in subcontracts.

Natural_Language: DHS and SSA may terminate a contractor's MOU and deny access to E-Verify in accordance with the terms of the MOU. Natural_Language: The contractor may request a price adjustment only after the effective date of a new annual E.O. minimum wage determination published pursuant to paragraph (a). Prices will be adjusted only for increased labor costs (including subcontractor labor costs) as a result of the annual E.O. minimum wage, and for associated labor costs (including those for subcontractors). Associated labor costs must include increases or decreases that result from changes in social security and unemployment taxes and workers' compensation insurance, but will not otherwise include any amount for general and administrative costs, overhead, or profit.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1904_b_1_a (request only after effective date of new determination); P_22_1904_b_1_b (adjust only for increased labor costs including subcontractor); P_22_1904_b_1_c (associated labor costs must include SS/unemployment/workers comp changes); P_22_1904_b_1_d (must not include G&A, overhead, or profit)
Validation_Notes: Mixed conjunctive with negation. 'Only after' = temporal conditional on (a). 'Must include' = mandatory conjunction. 'Will not include' = negation of G&A/overhead/profit. Permissive 'may request' governs contractor action but downstream adjustments are mandatory framework.

Natural_Language: The wage rate price adjustment under this clause is the lowest amount calculated by subtracting from the new E.O. wage rate the following: The current E.O. minimum wage rate; the current service or construction wage determination rate under the contract (if the wage rate is applicable to that worker); or the actual wage currently paid the worker. If the amount is zero or below, there will be no increase paid for this worker.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1904_b_2_a (adjustment = lowest of: new rate minus current E.O. rate, or current SCA/DBA rate, or actual wage); P_22_1904_b_2_b (if result <= 0, no increase)
Justification_Rules: Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Negation (Neg): Rule 10
Validation_Notes: Complex calculation methodology. The 'lowest amount' creates a disjunctive comparison but the result is a single mandatory value. Conditional negation for zero/negative results. HIGH-RISK due to Material Implication on the zero-or-below clause. Table examples in (b)(2)(i)-(ii) illustrate but do not add new requirements.

Natural_Language: Example 1: New E.O. wage rate $16.10, Previous E.O. rate $15.70, current SCA/DBA rate $15.75, actual wage $15.80. Calculation: $16.10 - $15.80 = $0.30. Price adjustment is $0.30.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1904_b_2_i (illustrative example showing positive price adjustment calculation)
Validation_Notes: Illustrative example demonstrating positive adjustment calculation. Not an independent requirement but operationalizes the formula in (b)(2). HIGH-RISK for implication structure.

Natural_Language: Example 2: New E.O. wage rate $15.50, Previous E.O. rate $15.10, current SCA/DBA rate $15.75, actual wage $15.80. Calculation: $15.50 - $15.80 = -$0.30. No price adjustment for this worker.
Atomic_Propositions: P_22_1904_b_2_ii (illustrative example showing no adjustment when result is negative)
Validation_Notes: Illustrative example demonstrating zero/negative result. Confirms the negation clause in (b)(2). Not independent requirement.
